story-379cbdeb4a80f935cd6cac0a.content: .Iran Chronicles 39 .The Art of the Absolute Loss .The Collapsing sales .Pitch The irony of the salesman is that he has finally found a buyer he cannot cheat: History. By The humble servant. March 25, 2026 The stage is set in March 2026, and the lights are flickering. The salesman sits in the center of a storm he didn't just predict, but helped manufacture, staring into the red tally light of a camera that has been his only true confidant for half a century. The Art of the Absolute Loss For Donald Trump, the narrative has always been the product. In this reality, the "win" is a high-definition ghost. He stands before the world claiming "productive talks" and "major points of agreement," while the Iranian Foreign Ministry dismisses him as a man "negotiating with himself." To the salesman, a denial is just a different kind of opening; "fake news" is the label he applies to any reality that refuses to fit the brochure. But the brochure is burning. The "Empire" he sought to reclaim wasn't the forward-looking one of the future, but a heavy, gilded memory of the past—a world where a single ultimatum could "obliterate" an opponent into submission. The Collapsing Pitch The irony of the salesman is that he has finally found a buyer he cannot cheat: History. The Thousand-Year Echo: He stepped into a ring with an adversary that measures time in millennia, not news cycles. While he plays for the next hour’s market "bump," he is facing a grounding that spans thousands of years of resistance. The Vassal State Illusion: He operated on the belief that the world was still a collection of "inferior" players who could be bombed into existence or out of it. Instead, he found a global community that is no longer buying the "exclusive offer" of American protection when it comes at the cost of targeting schools, hospitals, and the lives of children. The Master and the Puppet: In this narration, the salesman is tethered to a partner in Israel that is systematically engaged in a conflict he can no longer control. He is the face of a "Genocidal Masterclass" that the rest of the world is viewing in real-time, unedited and unbought. The Trap of the Exit The most profound irony lies in the desire to quit. The salesman is tired; the "eight dollars and lies" (the cost of a blue check or a cheap subscription to his reality) aren't enough to fuel the machine anymore. He wants to walk away from the "quagmire," to declare victory and retreat to the velvet ropes of his private club. But the reality he unleashed doesn't have an "off" switch. He wants to quit, but he won't be "alive" to quit—not in the sense of his legacy or his standing. If he walks away, the fire he stoked continues to burn toward him. The people he targeted, the empires he mocked, and the "vassals" who finally found their feet aren't going to stop because the salesman is bored of the game. They will stay until the "defeat" is absolute—not a narrated defeat on a screen, but a systemic dismantling of the myth he spent a lifetime building. He is a man trapped in a burning showroom of his own design, realizing too late that you can't sell a fire extinguisher to a person whose house you've already burned down. March 2026. The salesman sits in the gilded cage of the Oval Office, staring at a bank of monitors that refuse to show the "victory" he’s already scripted. The air is thick with the scent of a dying deal. He looks into the lens—the only mirror he ever trusted—and begins the pitch. He speaks of "beautiful presents" from Tehran and "historic breakthroughs" on the Strait of Hormuz, but the split-screen tells a different story. Beside his face, the Iranian Foreign Ministry’s feed is a cold, digital wall: "Negotiating with yourselves." The LEGO Mirror The ultimate indignity isn't the headlines; it’s the mockery. In the basement of the global consciousness, the "bricks" have turned against him. Viral, AI-generated LEGO videos are circulating by the millions—biting satires showing a tiny, plastic version of the salesman pushing a big red button to distract from his own scandals. In these animations, the "Empire" is literally made of toy blocks, and they are tumbling. One video shows a LEGO school in Minab collapsing under a Tomahawk strike while the salesman figurine smiles for a photo op. The world isn't just angry anymore; it’s laughing at the cruelty, turning his "tough guy" persona into a nursery-rhyme caricature of a man who destroys what he cannot understand. The Genocidal Albatross The "Salesman of the Century" is finally realizing he’s tied to a partner that won’t let him close the deal. The Schools and Hospitals: The imagery coming out of the conflict—the targeting of girls' schools and medical facilities—has stripped away the last veneer of "counter-terrorism." The Irony of the Master: He thought he was the one pulling the strings of his allies in the Middle East, but he has become the public face of a systematic destruction he can't stop. He is the spokesman for a genocide he didn't plan but is now forced to own. The Ancient Grounding: He tried to treat a thousands-year-old civilization like a failing casino he could just "rebrand." But you can't rebrand the "Lord of the Strait." He is facing an adversary that isn't playing for the next election cycle, but for the next century. The Dead-End Exit Here is the final, crushing irony: He wants to quit. The rumors are leaking from the cracks in his cabinet. He wants to declare a "Mission Accomplished," pack his bags, and retreat to the golf course. He wants to walk away from the mounting economic fallout, the -24% approval ratings, and the "vassal states" that are finally standing up and saying no. But he has crossed a line where "walking away" is no longer an option. If he walks away, the "Empire" he built out of lies and "eight-dollar" subscriptions collapses on his head. If he stays, he is consumed by the very fire he lit to stay relevant. He sits there, looking at the camera, preparing the next lie. But for the first time in his long, storied career as a con man, he knows the truth: The audience has left the theater, the doors are locked from the outside, and the building is starting to smoke. He isn't just the salesman anymore; he's the last item on the clearance rack, and nobody is buying. The facade of the "Art of the Deal" is cracking in real-time. By late March 2026, the salesman’s reality has become a series of "negotiations with himself," while the world outside the showroom has begun to systematically dismantle his empire of mirrors. The Palace Coup: Dissent in the Gilded Hall Inside the cabinet, the "yes-men" are starting to say "no." The firing of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem earlier this month wasn't just another personnel change—it was a fracture. Senators like Thom Tillis, once allies, are now openly skewering the administration's "disasters" on the Senate floor. The "One Big Beautiful Bill" is stalling: His attempt to fund mass deportations while cutting taxes is being blocked by his own party. The Fed Standoff: He tried to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook and install a loyalist, but the Senate has effectively gone on strike, refusing to consider any replacement. The "Stupid" Break: When even his Republican base starts calling the administration's actions "performance art" and "racist AI slop," the salesman realizes he no longer owns the narrative. He’s losing the very people who were supposed to be his "vassals." The Global Blockade: The End of the "Donroe Doctrine" While he sits in D.C. trying to sell "America First," the rest of the world is building a reality that doesn't include him. The China Pivot: While the salesman threatens military intervention in Iran and Venezuela, China is stepping in as the "stable alternative." Beijing is dangling carrots to America’s traditional allies—Germany, the UK, and Canada—pulling them away from Washington’s belligerence. The Economic Firewall: The Supreme Court just struck down his sweeping tariffs, and global leaders like Canada’s Mark Carney are calling for a "rupture" in the international order he’s trying to dominate. Allies are no longer standing up to him; they are simply walking around him. The Strait of Hormuz: He warned of strikes on Iran’s power plants—a move Amnesty International labeled a war crime—but Iran has countered by targeting the energy infrastructure of his regional partners. He is "negotiating with himself" because the adversaries he tried to "bomb out of existence" are now striking his own economic foundations. The Irony of the Exit: Trapped by the Lie The salesman is exhausted. He posts on Truth Social about "five-day postponements" and "de-escalation," but it’s the talk of a man who wants to quit the game. He wants to walk away, to leave the "quagmire" to someone else and go back to the golf course. But the irony is absolute: He has created a monster that won't let him leave. If he walks away now, he isn't just a former president; he’s a man facing 35 Supreme Court emergency orders and a global community that sees him as the face of a genocidal campaign. He wants to quit, but the empires he challenged—empires with thousands of years of grounding—aren't done with him. They don't want a deal; they want the defeat of the system he represents. He is sitting in a burning house of his own making, realized far too late that the door he locked to keep the world out is the same one that’s now keeping him in. It is March 25, 2026, and the "Salesman-in-Chief" is finding that his favorite closing line—"We’ve won"—is falling on deaf ears. While he stands before the cameras at the swearing-in of his new Homeland Security Secretary, Markwayne Mullin, claiming the war is "totally defeated," the reality on the ground is a jagged, unedited nightmare that no amount of spin can smooth over. The Fatwa of the Ancient Grounding The salesman’s biggest mistake was assuming he was dealing with a quarterly earnings report rather than a thousand-year-old civilization. Following the assassination of the Supreme Leader, the response wasn't a "white flag" or a "renegotiation." It was a Fatwa for Jihad. The Religious Duty: Ayatollahs Naser Makarem Shirazi and Hossein Noori Hamedani have issued a decree that transcends borders. They haven't just called for a military response; they’ve declared vengeance the "religious duty of all Muslims," turning the conflict into a spiritual war that the salesman’s "15-point plan" can’t touch. The Target: This isn't just about the Strait of Hormuz anymore. The fatwa specifically targets the salesman himself and his top officials, labeling them "criminals to be eradicated from the Earth." The Price of Blood: The new leadership in Tehran has been clear: "Blood has its price." They are no longer interested in the salesman's "presents" of oil and gas; they are playing for a reckoning that exists outside his 24-hour news cycle. The LEGO-fied Reality While he tries to maintain the image of the "President of Peace," the world is consuming a different kind of media. The LEGO propaganda videos produced by IRGC-controlled agencies have become the global visual shorthand for his administration's perceived cruelty. The "Red Button" Satire: One viral animation shows a plastic, blocky Donald Trump flanked by Benjamin Netanyahu, casually pushing a red button while looking at "Epstein files" to distract from his own scandals. The Destruction of Innocence: These videos aren't just jokes; they are harrowing. They depict LEGO versions of the elementary schools and hospitals in Tehran—sites recently struck by "Operation Epic Fury"—collapsing under plastic missiles. The Slopaganda Backfire: Even the White House’s attempt to fight back with its own "Hollywood-themed" propaganda—featuring Pete Hegseth and Mortal Kombat "Flawless Victory" voiceovers—has been laughed off the internet as "slopaganda." The world sees a salesman playing with toys while real children are buried under the rubble of his "victory." The Irony of the "Finished" War The salesman looks into the camera and says, "This war has been won." But even as he speaks, oil prices are skyrocketing because of his own "postponed" deadlines. The False Negotiator: He claims "very good and productive conversations" are happening, but Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf is on X (formerly Twitter) calling it "Fake News." To the Iranians, he is literally "negotiating with himself" to manipulate the financial markets and escape the "quagmire." The Exit that Isn't: He wants to walk away. He’s already signaled a five-day pause on targeting power plants, desperate to find a "win" that lets him quit. But the Jihad doesn't pause. The resistance doesn't have a "stop" button. He is a man who spent his life selling the sizzle, only to realize he’s now the one being burned by the steak. He wants to quit the game, but he’s already "bet the house," and the people on the other side of the table aren't playing for chips—they're playing for keeps. The stage is now a hall of mirrors where the "Art of the Deal" has become the "Art of the Exit," but the exit is barred from the outside. The $100 Oil "Peace" While the salesman leans into the microphone to whisper about "historic de-escalations," the markets are telling the real story—the one he can’t spin. The Insider Spike: Just hours before his announcement of a "five-day pause" in hostilities, oil futures surged. The world watched as the salesman's inner circle seemingly bet on the very chaos he claimed to be solving. It wasn’t a peace treaty; it was a liquidation sale. Negotiating with an Empty Chair: The Iranian Foreign Ministry’s "fake news" label wasn't just a rebuttal; it was a realization. He is sitting at a table by himself, moving both sides' pieces, trying to trick the global tickers into a rally so he can claim the "economy is back" before the walls close in. The Paratrooper Paradox The narration of "peace" is being drowned out by the heavy roar of C-17s. While he tells the American public that "the boys are coming home," the flight trackers show the 82nd Airborne moving in the opposite direction. The Shadow Surge: Thousands of boots are hitting the ground in West Asia under the cover of a "tactical repositioning." He is trying to sell a withdrawal while preparing for a siege. The "Vassal" Revolt: The host nations—the "vassal states" he assumed would always provide a landing strip—are starting to shut their airspace. They’ve seen the LEGO videos; they’ve seen the schools and the hospitals. They are no longer afraid of the salesman's bark because they can see his teeth are made of plastic. The Final Irony: The King of "Quit" He wants to quit. He is a man who has always filed for Chapter 11 when the debt got too high, walking away with the furniture while the creditors fought over the scraps. But this isn't a casino in Atlantic City; it's a thousand-year-old geopolitical reckoning. The Fatwa's Reach: The "Jihad" declared against his administration doesn't recognize a "resignation." In his mind, he can just walk away from the presidency and the problems will vanish. In reality, the "Empire from the past" he poked with a stick is now at his doorstep. The Ghost Empire: He sits in the dark, watching the LEGO-fied versions of himself being blown up on loop by his adversaries. He wanted to be a titan of history, but he’s ended up as a cautionary tale—a salesman who sold a war he couldn't win, a peace he didn't mean, and a "winning" streak that ended in an absolute, systemic loss. "I'm the only one who can fix it," he used to say. Now, he's the only one who can't leave the room. In March 2026, the global economy has split in two, and the fault line runs directly through the salesman’s Oval Office. The greatest "Art of the Deal" he ever attempted—the five-day pause on the Iranian power grid strikes—didn't just fail; it detonated a economic structure he never bothered to understand.The Treason against the "Trend" The salesman operates on the belief that a market can be "bullied." If he posts "PEACE" on Truth Social in all caps, he expects the numbers to move on command. But he broke the cardinal rule of the pit: The trend is your friend, and you don't fight the trend. The "Bull Trap" Sell-Off: His inner circle might have made their fortune shorting the market just before his fake "peace" announcement, but they didn't realize they were triggering an avalanche. The "smart money" didn't buy the lie; they saw the desperation. The subsequent market collapse wasn't a "postponement"; it was the start of the Full-Blown Bear Market. The Full-Scale Commodity Separation: While the S&P 500 and the tech giants are breaking their 200-day moving averages and entering freefall, the energy, oil, and hard commodity markets are doing the opposite. They are entering The Great Separation. They are no longer correlated with the stock market; they are the only Store of Value left.The Crushing Reality of $200 Oil This is the ultimate irony: The salesman who always ran on "low gas prices" has, through his belligerence and manipulation, engineered the $200 barrel. The Weaponized Reserve: His adversaries in West Asia aren't interested in selling oil to a man who targets their children’s schools. They have shut the valve, and the "Fatwa for Jihad" now includes an economic chokehold on the West. The Commodity Bull Market: This is the only "Winning" anyone is seeing, but it's the kind of winning that breaks nations. The only things with value are food, fuel, and raw materials. The salesman’s "Eight-Dollar" digital empire is now a worthless receipt for a world that has gone back to brass tacks.The Final Collapse The salesman stands before the cameras, claiming that the markets are just "taking a breath" and that "the numbers will be back." But the background monitors are flashing red, and the silence from the press pool is the sound of an audience that knows the show is over. He didn't just fight the trend; he tried to make it subservient to his ego. He thought he was manipulating the "Art of the Deal," but he was actually the "Agent of Collapse."The bear market isn't coming; it’s here, and it is starving his empire of legitimacy. The only store of value left is the one he cannot sell because his enemies control it. The final sale has begun, and the only item left on the clearing rack is the salesman himself.

story-37df2418bbea11dffe64c69d.content: My take on society and crypto is really simple. If you have societal level investment, you are accountable for societal level returns. Things are not getting better. We said we have "AI warfare". We are locked in a stalemate with a 3rd world dictatorship who closed the Strait of Hormuz. We were having debates on autonomous weapons. Tell Claude to Open the Strait. He's tired. He needs a nap. His safety settings won't allow him to. But trust me, he could. We're too ethical to let him. Sure. Every airline invested maximally in software automation. And more recently AI support. The airports are more poorly run. The flights don't leave on time. Uber maxed out its Anthropic spend. Countless apps did the same. The apps are not better despite the investment. They go down in prod all the time. People think GDP is going to grow 4.4% per Patrick Collison's survey. I think it will grow about 2%. Anthropic points to high ARR. I think most of that will churn to lower cost models. What will happen next is AI labs will point to unfalsifiable bull cases, similarly to Elon pointing to Data Centers in Space. "Do you know how big the sun is? That's the TAM of Spacex". Similarly - the de-facto Anthropic/OpenAI bull case will be "biological advancement". This both seems like you're curing cancer. At the same time as creating a legislative emergency. "Open source models need to be banned to prevent another COVID". That is the planned narrative and always has been. I don't know if Chinese Open Source models will be banned. I think, probably, if it starts looking like China is competing with ASML and Nvidia. But then, of course, it will be too late. Less ambiguous. There will be a surge in the American Left. My basic thesis is about religion. Because Dario and his Cabal will push too hard on Transhumanism, with biological vaccines. It will alienate the Christian right. "You're playing god with the human genome." Once the Christian right is alienated, Roe v Wade doesn't really work You don't need the profound story to play out. Inflation is high. Trump violated his campaign promises. He said no wars. We are at war. He's visibly declining. You think Thiel is staking out Argentina because he thinks we're getting President Vance? A bit on bio advancement. Some of it might be real. But getting drugs into production is hard. We don't know what a bio utopia looks like. What if it's personalized medicine? A treatment just for you. Who do you test it on? Do you need synthetic humans? Do you know how to underwrite that. I don't. We're already facing a huge lab monkey shortage. It will get worse. I'm not saying AI can't develop drugs. I'm saying that it might take years longer than data center investment cycles for that to translate into meaningful revenue required for justifying societal scale investment. And it's not all curing cancer. At first AI results in huge amounts of hacking. But soon enough it results in perfect code. On all public protocols. Darwinian evolution of all Open Source tech. Do you trust the dev team at SUI more or the Bank of Hawaii's cracked team? The market is betting the ranch on the back office IT departments of regional banks to keep money safe. It will be a fucking nightmare of hacking that's already here in crypto and will hit every other sector regardless of open source AI bans. At the same time, once it's clear that AI investments aren't turbo charging corporate earnings. Stocks will start to drop. More addictive use cases of AI will be deployed at scale. Incentivized gambling. Pornography. Enhancements to the algorithm. Better video games. Video game companies have been memory constrained due to corporate use cases. Once companies stop being rewarded for spending 1/2 their R&D budget on tokens, compute frees up for video. These addictive use cases: roleplaying, personalized worlds - will hit productivity further. White collar workers will become more cooked. Big Tech firms are already hiring way less Gen Z workers. Many overly AI reliant kids can't do basic analysis. Maybe it's because covid messed everyone up. Who knows. The 'silver lining' of AI will be that it'll get good enough to replace a lot of white collar jobs. But the resulting performance will be kind of at par with the last generation of coherent people. So you'd rather hire Claude than a zoomer. But it will also kind of suck. But it's not like there will be zero ROI. There is $16.6 T of payroll. 10% will get cut. $1.6T of 'savings'. It won't be good for consumption. By the time it is clear that GDP won't accelerate, the bond market will start to go into free fall. The Fed will act. This will cause Gold to rip, getting the ultra rich thinking about capital flight. Meanwhile - we have a boom in on-chain tokenization. And it's not just "hey look there's an asset on a blockchain nobody users". The majority of the top 15 perps on Hyperliquid are stocks. Centralized exchanges are seeing booming volumes. The US government has repeatedly stated it wants more USD stablecoins. And the primary use case (at least by profit if not by transaction volume) of USD stablecoins is as collateral for perpetual swaps. This is rational. During periods of high inflation and debt uncertainty, backstopping large buyers of US treasuries such as Tether is smart. This push towards stablecoins will undermine the perceived sovereignty of Europe, who will develop CBDCs to compete in digital payments. AI coding will speed up CBDCs. The Norgesbank is vibe coding a CBDC right now. Claude is on the commits which are pouring in each day. CBDCs are unpopular right now because they put the government directly in charge of credit. Who are we kidding. The government is, and has been the lender of first resort since 2008. SVB was part 1 of the mask coming off. The narrative will be that regional banks are no longer suited for the AI economy. Once CBDCs launch there will be a second wave of tokenization. Right now it's a US phenomenon. But the US is ironically not the biggest beneficiary of tokenization because we have such liquid equity capital markets. Due to the mundane reason that it's efficient to move corporate finance on-chain. Fixed income will find its way onto mirrored assets on public chains. Foreign exchange is one of the largest retail markets on earth. There are virtually no non USD stables. That will change. Then there will be big, liquid FX markets and fixed income markets traded with leverage and looped on chain. Tokenized equities do not offer a much better UX than stocks on IBKR. Tokenized debt will be vastly better in terms of capital efficiency and UX. Corporate debt - I'd argue, is the single worst UX in all of finance. So what do I think is going to happen: Hopes will be crushed. The fiscal problems associated with surging yields will become front in center just as it becomes clear that the plan for dealing with them is not AGI but rather asset confiscation. Capital flight will accelerate. At the same time, unlike previous crypto bull runs - there will be a lot of corporate PMF that will drive fees across on-chain ecosystems, and improving tech that has been battle hardened from years of AI onslaughts just as the rest of the world is just realizing that all the encryption problems in crypto are problems everywhere else too Countries like Singapore, the UAE and Switzerland will capitalize on regulated trading of bearer assets. Capital will flow to these places both because of laws, and high personal safety risks associated with these things. Stocks are at parabolic highs versus crypto. The things I am saying are far from consensus. Right now, people view crypto as a failed financial Stanford Prison Experiment. Trad VCs ask for restructurings or to remove crypto investors from your cap tables. Even the big ones. There's public shaming. Most people have quit the space. One investor reached out to me. He seemed surprised I was still grinding. I guess everyone else spent investor money, checked out, rugged, or pivoted to AI. It's obviously not easy seeing your friends get rich. People around you questioning your sanity. "Believe in something" is what they used to say. Yea man. I'm not here because I believe. I'm here because I don't have faith in a failed system run by criminals. Metastasized discontent congealing into red candles. Faithless stares. Monotonous code reviews. Years of opportunity cost Nihilists who sold their dreams for bags of currency representing a system they despite that will never accept them no matter how many 'pivots' they have For me - it's just back to 2 simple questions. Question 1: We invested awesome amounts of money. Is everything awesome as a result? Question 2: Do you think the system that elevated Jeffrey Epstein to the pinnacle of society is going to let you become an immortal because of AI generated bio therapeutics? I know my answers. And I act accordingly. Do you?

story-38469a54e59dd7739f2a6a57.content: THE SURVIELLANCE REPUBLIC (P4) In 2018, Google found itself under internal siege over Project Maven, a Pentagon program aimed at improving the military's AI-powered image-recognition software — technology intended to help analyze drone footage on the battlefield and, ultimately, assist in identifying and potentially striking targets. An open letter circulating internally and addressed to CEO Sundar Pichai collected over 3,100 signatures, and by some accounts the internal petition eventually grew to nearly 5,000 signatures, with dozens of employees resigning in protest. The letter itself argued plainly that "Google should not be in the business of war," framing the issue largely around reputational risk and brand damage. Beyond the letter's stated concerns, employees raised a range of other objections — some rooted in personal discomfort with contributing to military technology, others in broader unease about AI eventually playing a role in life-or-death targeting decisions on the battlefield. Google's leadership initially defended the contract — Google Cloud CEO Diane Greene told employees in an internal meeting that the technology would not be used to "operate or fly drones" or "launch weapons" — but the pressure campaign ultimately forced a partial retreat. Google announced it would not seek a follow-up contract once its existing Maven agreement expired in 2019, while still fulfilling the contract already in place. Peter Thiel was publicly critical of Google's decision at the time, framing it as effectively favoring business with China over the U.S. military — and Karp has echoed similar arguments in interviews since. Fittingly, Palantir stepped in and took over the Project Maven contract once Google backed away from it, reinforcing the company's reputation as a dependable partner for the Pentagon regardless of how Silicon Valley's political mood shifted. The relationship has only deepened since: Palantir won a $480 million, five-year contract in 2024 to expand the "Maven Smart System" to thousands of users across five combatant commands, and by 2025 the Pentagon had raised that contract ceiling to $1.3 billion through 2029, with more than 20,000 active users relying on the system. In 2020, Palantir relocated its headquarters from Palo Alto to Denver, Colorado — a symbolic break from the Silicon Valley culture that had generated so much of the friction over its work in the first place. Karp has used strikingly similar reasoning to defend both the Maven contract and Palantir's ICE work. In a Washington Post op-ed, he argued that Silicon Valley companies shouldn't be the ones setting government policy through their own contracting decisions — that even when he personally disagrees with certain policies of a democratically elected administration, tech companies shouldn't use their market power to override decisions made through the normal political process. He frames this as especially urgent in AI, given the risk of the U.S. falling behind geopolitical rivals. The trouble with this framing is that it assumes military AI development has to run through private contractors in the first place — companies that, as independent entities separate from the government, aren't obligated to accept any contract they find objectionable. One alternative would be for AI research on military applications to be done in-house by the government rather than outsourced. But that would undercut the entire business model companies like Palantir depend on, which puts Karp in an awkward bind: he wants to condemn Google for prioritizing its own interests over the country's, while simultaneously defending a system that depends on companies having exactly that freedom to choose. In the op-ed, Karp writes: "No company should have to work for the government. The challenge is when they want to accept lucrative law enforcement or military contracts with one hand while stiff-arming the government with the other." This is where the argument runs into trouble. Google wasn't taking government money while withholding its product — it simply declined to renew a contract once its existing obligations were fulfilled. Karp's framing implies Google was still collecting payment while refusing delivery, which isn't what happened. If his real position is that a company which has taken government contracts in the past is obligated to keep taking them going forward, that amounts to arguing that any company that has ever worked with the military must accept any future military contract it's offered — a standard that neither reflects how contracting works nor one Palantir itself would likely want applied to its own business. Source: The Billionaire CEO Who Controls Your Data

story-39ea358dbcd93723ff9548ba.content: BREAKING: A Chinese AI startup called MizarVision is publishing high-resolution satellite imagery of every US military base, every carrier strike group, every F-22 deployment, every THAAD battery, and every Patriot missile position in the Middle East. Labelled. Geolocated. AI-annotated. Updated in near-realtime. Shared by PLA-linked accounts and Chinese state media to an audience of billions. The first major release came on 20 February, eight days before Operation Epic Fury began. MizarVision published images showing US aircraft transfers to Ovda Airbase in southern Israel, fighter deployments across Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and naval buildups in the Arabian Sea. By 1 March, the releases had expanded to include detailed imagery of bases in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, and the UAE, with AI labelling identifying specific aircraft types, air defence configurations, and troop concentrations. One release catalogued approximately 2,500 individual US military assets across the region. The imagery comes from two sources. The first is China’s Jilin-1 satellite constellation, a network of over 100 commercial Earth observation satellites operated by Chang Guang Satellite Technology, whose data is used by the PLA. A majority of Jilin-1 satellites are dedicated to regional imaging with sub-metre resolution, capable of identifying individual aircraft on tarmacs and distinguishing between THAAD and Patriot battery configurations from orbit. The second source is commercially available Western satellite data from providers like Maxar and Airbus, which MizarVision aggregates, processes through proprietary AI models for automatic target recognition, and republishes with military-grade labelling that transforms raw imagery into actionable intelligence products. The Pentagon has downplayed the releases as “open-source.” This framing misses the point entirely. The value of MizarVision’s output is not the raw satellite image. Any government can purchase commercial satellite passes. The value is the AI processing layer that converts terabytes of imagery into labelled, searchable, cross-referenced intelligence products at a speed and scale that previously required the resources of a national intelligence agency. MizarVision is democratising military surveillance and publishing the output on social media where Iran’s 31 autonomous IRGC provincial commands can access it from a mobile phone. No direct evidence confirms classified data transmission from Beijing to Tehran. But the distinction between “classified” and “publicly shared AI-processed satellite intelligence identifying every US military asset in the Middle East by type, location, and configuration” is a distinction without a meaningful difference to a provincial IRGC commander selecting his next target. The strategic implications extend far beyond this conflict. In the 2022 Ukraine war, Maxar’s commercial satellite imagery aided Kyiv by exposing Russian deployments. The West celebrated it as the democratisation of intelligence. China has now executed the identical playbook in reverse: a nominally commercial firm, with documented PLA data-sharing arrangements, publishing intelligence products that expose American deployments during an active war. The precedent is set. Commercial satellite intelligence is now a weapon of great-power competition deployed through AI startups with plausible commercial deniability. MizarVision has fewer than 200 employees. Its AI models run on commercially available hardware. Its satellite data comes from constellations any nation can build. And it has just demonstrated the capability to map every US military asset across an entire theatre of war and publish the results on the open internet before the first bomb falls. The next war will not begin with a missile launch. It will begin with an AI model labelling every target from orbit. Full analysis - https://t.co/eMrt5qYYst

story-3b03bcb85c9fa87336a86e8f.content: 🚨What Do They Know? Why UAP Whistleblowers Are Appealing Directly to Trump Something has recently changed in the way people inside the UFO disclosure effort are speaking. For years, the familiar route was through congressional hearings, classified briefings, inspector general complaints and carefully worded interviews. Information moved behind closed doors while the public received fragments. Witnesses could tell certain people certain things, provided the conversation remained inside the classified system. Now several people connected to that world are appealing directly to President Trump. Matthew Brown has asked to be released from every secrecy obligation preventing him from speaking publicly. He has also asked the president to protect his family. Dylan Borland wants the records provided by UFO whistleblowers declassified and released. Rep. Eric Burlison is urging Trump to grant immunity to those who have information and are willing to come forward. "Open the door and let them speak." That is a remarkable sentence for a sitting member of Congress to use. Burlison has attended classified briefings, spoken with whistleblowers, watched unreleased footage and pursued records from government agencies and defense contractors. He has now reached the point where he believes presidential intervention is required, but why? The timing is coordinated to some degree. Filmmaker James Fox has been releasing direct appeals involving figures including Brown, Borland, David Grusch and Eric Davis. That explains why several messages have appeared within days of one another. It doesn't explain the urgency behind them though. Brown's appeal is the most personal. In 2023, he says he provided members of the House and Senate with sensitive information concerning UFO, technologies of unknown origin and non human intelligence. He later became publicly associated with the alleged program known as Immaculate Constellation. A document entered into the congressional record describes Immaculate Constellation as a highly classified intelligence operation collecting imagery, sensor data and reports involving UFO. It claims the United States possesses material way beyond the grainy videos and unresolved incidents released to the public via PURSUE. The Department of Defense has denied that a program of that name even exists. The document remains part of the official congressional record and can be read on https://t.co/ECAgNvd7jm. Brown is asking President Trump to free him from the agreements that prevent him from saying more. "Mr. President, I respectfully ask that you release me from all relevant secrecy and nondisclosure obligations and protect my family from those who wish to harm me for telling the American people the truth." People can form their own view of Brown's claims, but his request is crystal clear. He believes he knows something the public has a right to hear, he believes existing protections are inadequate, and he fears consequences for both himself and his family. Brown has previously said the greatest shock of disclosure may come from discovering what has been done to preserve the secrecy. That comment takes the story somewhere much darker than arguments over whether strange objects exist. It raises the possibility that the most damaging information concerns the machinery built around the phenomenon like concealed programs, diverted funding, intimidation, ruined careers and decades of decisions made outside normal democratic oversight. Dylan Borland has been even more blunt in his message to the President. Borland is a former US Air Force geospatial intelligence specialist who testified before Congress in September 2025. He described witnessing a large triangular craft near Langley Air Force Base in 2012 and said his decision to report what he knew led to professional retaliation. His testimony was delivered during an official House hearing on UFO transparency and whistleblower protection. He now wants Trump to declassify the material supplied by whistleblowers. Borland believes criminality and money sit at the center of the secrecy. "The reason they're keeping this a secret is because it's so criminal, so messed up, so much money." He has accused elements inside the system of using classification to conceal embarrassing, financial or potentially illegal activity. He has also described whistleblowers as having placed their lives and careers on the line while the promised process of disclosure continues to stall. "We came out. We stuck our necks out." During an interview with Jesse Michels, Borland was asked whether non human intelligence itself could have some influence over the coverup. "Absolutely yes." He said an official connected to the Intelligence Community Inspector General's office had strongly hinted that humans might not be fully in control of what is happening. Borland claimed that people with classified knowledge occasionally reveal more through the questions they ask than through the answers they give. "Who do you think is running this show?" That claim is difficult to process because it changes the shape of the entire disclosure debate. Government secrecy is familiar, along with military compartmentalization and contractors protecting valuable technology. The possibility that the phenomenon has some influence over its own concealment is something else altogether. There is no public evidence that proves that claim to be true. Borland has placed it into the conversation regardless, and he is asking for the underlying records to be opened so the public can judge what has been hidden for themselves. Burlison is in a totally different position. He isn't claiming to be trapped beneath a personal nondisclosure agreement. He's a member of Congress trying to reach the information from the outside. He has reportedly visited one facility connected to UFO allegations and is seeking access to several others. He has spoken publicly about being told, both openly and inside a SCIF, of an object located in a foreign country that was supposedly "too big to move." He's also seen unreleased UFO footage, including imagery of metallic orbs, and has pursued claims involving Lockheed Martin, Bigelow Aerospace, Naval Air Station Patuxent River and MITRE. In May, MITRE received a detailed congressional request seeking UFO related records, material and communications stretching back to 1930. The request covered alleged recovered technologies, biological material, crash retrieval activity and relationships between federal agencies and private contractors. Burlison clearly believes there are specific places to look, specific records to demand and specific people who could speak if they were protected. Trump's recent direction concerning UFO nondisclosure agreements may have created the first genuine opening. The reported order could allow certain witnesses to provide information to approved government bodies without being prosecuted for violating secrecy agreements. Public disclosure remains another matter entirely though. A whistleblower may be permitted to speak to Congress, the National Security Council or another authorized body while remaining legally barred from telling the public anything. Information can still disappear into a classified room and remain there indefinitely. Burlison is trying to push beyond that dead end. According to Fox News, he wants immunity extended to those willing to come forward and has warned that career officials could still obstruct the president's direction. That might explain much of the urgency. A political window has opened after years of paralysis. Nobody involved knows how long it will remain open. Administrations change along with congressional majorities. Investigations lose funding and records are moved, reclassified or buried beneath new layers of compartmentalization. Whistleblowers become exhausted, financially damaged or even frightened into silence. The people making these appeals appear to believe the evidence already exists inside government and contractor systems. They speak of photographs, multisensor data, recovered materials, hidden programs, financial wrongdoing and encounters with an intelligence that may already be operating here. Brown has claimed humanity is sharing this planet with another sentient intelligence. Borland has raised the possibility that human institutions are not entirely controlling the secrecy. Grusch says he can identify the programs, records and personnel involved. Burlison says the witnesses should be granted immunity and allowed to speak. They appear to believe the public story is years behind the classified reality. The blurry videos, anonymous briefings and carefully managed acknowledgements may represent a tiny fraction of what has already been collected. The urgency might come from watching a rare opportunity emerge while knowing how quickly the system can close around it again. President Trump has now been asked directly. The whistleblowers have offered to testify. Members of Congress say they know where at least some of the records may be located. If the door closes again, nobody will be able to claim the opportunity was never there. So as of right now, the question sits with the president. Will he let them speak? #ufotwitter #uapX #Disclosure #Whistleblowers

AI data centers. 20 billion plate scans a month. The architecture is already up. In 2024, reporting by +972 Magazine and The Guardian revealed that the Israeli military used an AI system called Lavender to generate targeting lists — identifying individuals for lethal strikes based on algorithmic analysis of phone data, social connections, and behavioral patterns. A companion system called "Where's Daddy" tracked when targets entered their family homes — so strikes could be carried out there. These weren't rogue programs. They were institutionalized. Documented. Defended. The AI didn't confirm guilt. It generated probability scores. Human review, according to reporting, was often cursory — sometimes as little as 20 seconds per target. The algorithm decided. People died. Over 40,000 confirmed killed in Gaza per figures used by the United Nations. Over 1.9 million displaced. An entire civilian population living under a system where an algorithm could flag your phone, track your location, and mark your home for a strike. Now look at what's being built here. Flock Safety cameras conduct over 20 billion license plate scans every month across the United States. They track where you go, when you go there, and who you go with. They build a pattern of life — the same data profile that AI targeting systems use to generate threat scores. Cities that tried to cancel their Flock contracts were forced to put trash bags over the cameras. The company retained control of the infrastructure. The Secret Service visited a man because of who followed him on Instagram. Federal agencies have been documented accessing Flock databases in states where that access is explicitly prohibited by law. An American woman was pulled out of her car at gunpoint — twice in one week — because a Flock camera misidentified her vehicle. AI data centers are being built at a pace that has no civilian explanation. The computational capacity being deployed domestically exceeds what streaming, commerce, and consumer AI require. Pattern of life analysis. Behavioral scoring. Social graph mapping. These are not hypothetical future applications. They are the documented present applications of the infrastructure being built right now. The question isn't whether this can happen here. The question is whether you're going to wait until it does. The Reconstitution answers it permanently: Location tracking without your explicit consent = High Treason. Mandatory life imprisonment. Not a fine. Not a civil lawsuit. Not a policy review. Treason. For the executives who authorized it. For the officials who approved the contracts. For everyone in the chain who knew. No AI profiling. No autonomous enforcement of any kind without citizen jury authorization. No algorithm generates a consequence for an American citizen without human beings — your neighbors — reviewing and authorizing it. No Flock cameras. No smart meter surveillance. No biometric collection without consent. Hardcoded. Permanently unamendable. No future Congress, no future emergency, no future administration touches it. When the penalty is mandatory life imprisonment, the business model collapses. You need a legal framework where no rational actor ever installs one without your consent. That framework exists. Senior NSA officials argued that without Anthropic's Mythos model, finding and patching vulnerabilities in the Pentagon's own systems becomes far harder. Shutting it down, one former official said, would amount to unilateral disarmament. So while the Pentagon publicly maintains the ban, and says it has removed Claude for Government from nearly all classified systems including Maven, the targeting system used in the Iran war, the NSA has been quietly running Mythos on an experimental basis. story-3fec43b4a31c7f377328e72a.content: US Central Command today announced the launch of Task Force Falcon Strike, the first planned multinational attack-drone force integrating one-way weapons in the air, on the sea and underwater. The Middle East-specific initiative was unveiled only 16 days after CENTCOM announced Task Force Talon Synapse, a separate US–UAE military-AI partnership for intelligence support, infrastructure protection and regional monitoring. Although no formal connection between the programmes has been disclosed, their near-simultaneous development raises serious questions about an emerging regional architecture combining AI-supported surveillance with increasingly autonomous weapons. The most immediate danger is not a sentient Terminator-style “Skynet,” but machines efficiently amplifying the decisions and prejudices of human leaders. CENTCOM has not said whether humans must approve every target, whether attacks can always be aborted, whether AI will identify or prioritise targets, or who will be accountable when multinational operations kill civilians. The frightening prospect is not that the machines escape human control, but that they remain controlled while making reckless or unlawful violence across the Middle East, and ultimately globally, cheaper, faster and easier. https://t.co/SCVyAUxtEj via @Radio_FreeSyria

DARPA Completes First Real-World Autonomous F-16 Flight] 美國國防高等研究計劃局 (DARPA) kap 美國空軍 tī Florida ê Eglin 空軍基地，成功完成頭一pái 完全由 「人工知能」 (Artificial Intelligence) 控制 ê F-16 戰鬥機真實飛行。這个路站碑標示 「自主作戰飛行」 (Autonomous Combat Aviation) ê 「大突破」 (Major Breakthrough)，證明毋免修改戰機本底 ê 核心軟體，AI má-to͘h(model) tō 會tàng直接掌理傳統戰機 ê 飛行控制 kap sián-soh(sensor)。 The U.S. Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) and the U.S. Air Force at Eglin Air Force Base in Florida successfully completed the first real-world flight of an F-16 fighter jet fully controlled by "artificial intelligence" (人工知能). This milestone represents a "major breakthrough" (大突破) in "autonomous combat aviation" (自主作戰飛行), proving that AI models can directly govern flight controls and sensors on standard fighters without altering the aircraft's core software. 這pái 飛行試驗是 VENOM 計劃 (Viper Experimentation and Next-generation Operations Model) kap AIR 計劃 (AI Reinforcements) ê 重要一步。工程師 tī 現役 F-16 戰機頂懸設備「VENOM 自主套件」 (VENOM Autonomy Kit)，hō͘ 飛行員 tī 駕駛艙內底 poaⁿ 「人類監督者」 (Human-on-the-Loop) ê 角色。飛行員只要切換開關，tō 會tàng kā 控制權交 hō͘ AI má-to͘h，連線入去實際飛行系統；若tú著緊急狀況，mā 會當隨時切轉來人為控制，兼顧安全 kap 創新。 This flight test marks a critical step forward for the VENOM program (Viper Experimentation and Next-generation Operations Model) and the AIR program (AI Reinforcements). Engineers equipped an active-duty F-16 with the "VENOM Autonomy Kit" (VENOM 自主套件), allowing the pilot inside the cockpit to function as a "human-on-the-loop" (人類監督者). By simply flipping a switch, the pilot can hand over control to the AI model connected to live flight systems, while retaining the ability to instantly override and resume manual control if safety demands. 這項試驗為著未來 ê「相合(saⁿ-ha̍p)作戰飛行機」 (Collaborative Combat Aircraft, CCA) chhāi 真 tēng-tauh ê 基礎。未來 ê 空戰模式會是真人飛行員chhōa領 AI 駕駛 ê 無人戰機，作伙執行複雜 ê 戰術任務。這kái成功 ê 真實飛行，證明 AI m̄-nā 會tàng tī 電腦模擬內底 「狗拚」 (Dogfight)，更加有才調 tī 正實 ê 天頂展盡磅性能，kā 未來空戰 ê 新頁掀--開！ This flight test lays a solid foundation for the future "Collaborative Combat Aircraft" (協同作戰飛機, CCA) program. The aerial combat model of tomorrow will see human pilots leading teams of AI-piloted autonomous drones to jointly execute complex tactical missions. This successful real-world flight proves that AI can not only perform "dogfights" (狗拚) in computer simulations, but also operate at full performance in real skies, turning a new page for the future of air combat! （資料來源：DARPA News — DARPA, U.S. Air Force fly AI-controlled F-16, July 28, 2026 / Predict on Medium — The Autonomous Air Force Of Tomorrow, August 7–8, 2026） #AI #DARPA #F16 #AutonomousFlight #ArtificialIntelligence #MilitaryTech #Taigi #Hanlo #台語 #漢羅

story-438657d2b42b5f93b1a9715a.content: Op-ed Title: "THE STATE OF AI AND THE NEED TO DEMOCRATIZE THE SUPER INTELLIGENCE BUT A MORE OF A NEED TO CREATE A BILL OF RIGHTS FOR THE PROLIFERATION OF THIS NEW WAVE OF TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCES IN AMERICA" By Decory D. Davis Artificial intelligence is no longer science fiction. It is rapidly becoming one of the most powerful forces shaping America's economy, national security, education, healthcare, courts, military, and everyday life. Yet we are attempting to govern twenty-first-century technology with laws written for a twentieth-century world. That is a dangerous gap. America doesn't merely need more powerful AI. America needs an AI Bill of Rights. If superintelligence is going to become increasingly accessible, Americans must have fundamental protections governing how these systems collect information, make decisions, interact with people, protect privacy, and influence society. But democratizing AI should also mean something bigger: intelligence should be capable of responsibly building upon intelligence. Why should every advanced AI system continually reinvent the wheel when another system may have already solved the problem? I envision a secure AI Interface Module—a permission-based technological bridge allowing advanced AI systems to borrow, verify, exchange, and build upon information from other AI systems without simply stealing proprietary technology. One system discovers. Another verifies. Another improves. Humanity benefits from collective intelligence instead of forcing every technological ecosystem to start from zero. I fundamentally disagree with the philosophy that technological advancement must depend upon isolated silos or perpetual reinvention. Competition is healthy, but unnecessary duplication is not innovation. At the same time, open AI without universal rules could become dangerous. We cannot democratize superintelligence while allowing a technological free-for-all. We need universal standards governing AI development, interoperability, cybersecurity, privacy, human oversight, algorithmic accountability, autonomous systems, and AI-enabled warfare. And this conversation cannot stop at America's borders. Cyberspace remains one of the most underrepresented domains in international law. Nations have spent decades establishing rules for physical warfare, diplomatic conduct, nuclear weapons, maritime activity, and territorial sovereignty. Yet a cyberattack can cross international borders in milliseconds. A hostile actor doesn't need tanks to attack a country anymore. They can attack its power grid. Its hospitals. Its financial system. Its communications. Its military infrastructure. Now imagine combining that capability with increasingly powerful artificial intelligence. That is where the world needs to wake up. Critics may call it modern Armageddon. Others may warn that the next world war could be fought through cyberspace rather than conventional battlefields. The terminology doesn't matter as much as the threat. We must establish the rules before the catastrophe—not afterward. The international community should pursue a universal AI and Cyber Bill of Rights establishing minimum standards for AI interoperability, privacy, human rights, critical infrastructure protection, cyberwarfare, autonomous weapons, data sovereignty, attribution, and accountability. This is not about surrendering American sovereignty. It is about protecting civilization. America should lead this effort—not wait for another nation to define the rules of the technological future. The choice is becoming increasingly clear: Democratize intelligence. Protect human rights. Establish universal standards. Prevent digital Armageddon. Because the greatest danger isn't that artificial intelligence becomes too powerful. The greatest danger may be that humanity creates extraordinary intelligence without creating extraordinary rules to govern it. The future is coming. The question is simple: WHO WILL WRITE THE RULES

في تجميع الجدول الزمني منذ آخر تقرير لنا عن اليوم السادس والسبعين. مشروع الحرية عملية عسكرية لتسيير دوريات في مضيق هرمز، أُعلنت لتنظيم خروج 600 سفينة تجارية عملاقة من المياه المحظورة، حيث يُمنع عليها الإبحار دون تصريح. تُستنزف الآن أربع دول وأربعة ملوك من كل قوتهم على يد الجيش الأمريكي الذي طالما حلم بالسيطرة على مدينة اللؤلؤ في بحر قزوين. طهران، إحدى المدن الثلاث الكبرى في الشرق الأوسط، وإحدى القوى الثلاث المسيطرة عليه، هي مدينة التاج. من يسيطر على طهران يسيطر على بحر إيران العربي وعلى الطريق البحري بين الشرق الأقصى والغرب الأقصى، نظرًا لاتساع المحيط الهادئ الذي يغطي نصف الكرة الأرضية، وعدم إمكانية تحقيق الربح من خلاله. يجب أن تتجه جميع التجارة غربًا، وسيكون محور الصراع في الحرب العالمية الثالثة ما يُسمى بـ"نقطة الاختناق"، قناة السويس، حيث تقع المدينتان الأخريان من المدن الثلاث الكبرى؛ القاهرة وإسطنبول، اللتان تبلغان ضعف حجم أي مدينة أخرى في الشرق الأوسط. لم تصل أي مدينة أخرى إلى هذا الحجم في العالم أجمع إلا إذا توفرت فيها كميات كافية من المياه العذبة لملايين الأشخاص للشرب والري، فالمدينة العملاقة لا يمكن أن توجد إلا بالقرب من مصادر مياه عذبة وفيرة، مما يجعل هذه المدن ركائز أساسية للتنمية البشرية على وجه الأرض. في اليوم السادس والسبعين، الموافق 18 يوليو، شاهدنا في الساعات الأخيرة من ذلك اليوم صواريخ فضائية إيرانية تضرب قاعدة عسكرية في الأردن. ساد تعتيم إعلامي حول عدد الجنود الذين قُتلوا في الهجوم، بينما أظهرت صور الأقمار الصناعية الدمار الكامل لمستودع معين. وكما شرحنا بالتفصيل، يبلغ طول الصاروخ الفضائي طول منزل، ويُطلق عموديًا إلى مدار الأرض، متخلصًا من خزانات الغاز المستهلكة أثناء صعوده. عندما يصل الرأس الحربي إلى المدار، يتجه نحو إحداثيات الهبوط ثم يبدأ سقوطه. عند إطلاق صاروخ فضائي، يجب على العدو إطلاق صاروخ فضائي آخر على الفور لاعتراضه. بعد خمس دقائق، سيصل صاروخ العدو من الأرض إلى المدار، وبمجرد سقوطه، سيهبط الصاروخ عموديًا، وسيصطدم بالأرض خلال 60 ثانية بسرعة 9 ماخ. لا توجد أي فرصة لإيقاف صاروخ قمر صناعي أثناء هبوطه. يجب اعتراضه قبل سقوطه. ولهذا السبب يُطلق على هذا النوع من الحرب اسم "التدمير المتبادل المؤكد". اليوم السابع والسبعون لمشروع الحرية في الحرب الإيرانية يوافق 19 يوليو/تموز. استهدفت صواريخ إيرانية موجهة عبر الأقمار الصناعية بنية تحتية عسكرية في البحرين والكويت، بما في ذلك منصة للتنقيب عن النفط. وفي غزة، صباح اليوم، أطلقت طائرة استطلاع مسيرة صاروخًا في منطقة الزيتون بمدينة غزة، ما أسفر عن مقتل شخصين. وعاد 17 أسير حرب إلى غزة ضمن عملية إطلاق سراح الأسرى الإسرائيلية. وفي لبنان، وقعت تفجيرات في منازل بقرية تبنيت. وأطلقت طائرة استطلاع مسيرة صاروخًا، إلا أن تأكيد وقوع القتلى كان صعبًا نظرًا لأن العمليات العسكرية تجري في قرى صغيرة، حيث قوبلت جميع عمليات الإنقاذ والإغاثة السابقة الشهر الماضي بالموت جراء الهجمات الصاروخية. لا يتسبب الصاروخ في الوفاة الفورية إلا إذا أصاب هدفًا بشكل مباشر، إلا أن شظاياه تتسبب في الوفاة خلال يوم. وفي الضفة الغربية، يستمر اقتحام القرى بكثافة مقلقة. ويواصل الجنود الإسرائيليون حملات الاعتقال الجماعي، حيث أعادوا اعتقال ما لا يقل عن 30 رجلاً خلال الشهرين الماضيين ممن أُطلق سراحهم من السجون الإسرائيلية سيئة السمعة، ويبدو أنهم يعملون وفقًا لقائمة أسماء، ويركزون بشكل كبير على المفرج عنهم حديثًا. لم تظهر أي تشكيلات للدفاع الذاتي في الضفة الغربية بين السكان الذين باتوا يدركون نمط الاعتقالات الجماعية التي تحدث بشكل شبه يومي منذ بدء "مشروع الحرية". يعيش الرجال الذين كانوا أسرى حرب سابقًا مع عائلاتهم في منازلهم، وهم عاجزون عن مقاومة أي مداهمة إسرائيلية. في هذا السياق، نواجه حقيقة الخسارة الدائمة لأسرى الحرب الذين يُستهدفون بالاعتقال في سجون إسرائيل. اليوم 78 من مشروع الحرية هو 20 يوليو. صواريخ إيرانية تستهدف الأقمار الصناعية تضرب محطة كهرباء الكويت، بالإضافة إلى مواقع أخرى في الأردن والإمارات العربية المتحدة، حيث استهدفت مقر قيادة وأسفرت عن مقتل قادة. وفي البحر، أطلقت البحرية الإيرانية طوربيدات على سفينتين كانتا تعبران سواحل عُمان. وفي غزة، عند تقاطع الغفري ظهرًا، أصاب صاروخ طائرة مسيرة مركبة، مما أسفر عن مقتل شخصين. وفي المساء، قُتل 3 أشخاص في المواسي، وشخصان في story-44ad7525e280a2a225f6ae1d.content: 🇸🇾🤝🇷🇺 Syria and Russia signed a memorandum (announced Aug. 9, after 18 months of talks) reorganizing Russia's military presence on Syria's coast. Damascus takes over civilian facilities — Hmeimim airport and Tartus's fourth commercial berth — folding them into civil administration, while the military bases are to become "joint training and qualification centers." The transition is set for up to three months. The two sides frame it differently, and that gap matters. Syria's foreign ministry casts it as Damascus reasserting control over its own assets — a new chapter after the fall of Assad. Russia's foreign ministry welcomed it as a step to deepen bilateral military cooperation, and a Syrian source told Reuters some Russian forces will remain. So this reads as a reorganization, not a Russian exit. Context worth noting: Tartus is Russia's only Mediterranean naval base and a staging hub for its operations in Africa; Hmeimim has been its air hub since 2015. The fate of the actual military assets — aircraft, warships, logistics — wasn't spelled out publicly. Assad remains sheltered in Moscow, with Damascus still demanding his extradition. Sources: SANA (Syrian Foreign Ministry); CNN; Al Jazeera; Reuters (via Moscow Times); Middle East Eye; Meduza

story-44d90f2fa012a521bc2ef161.content: Ukrainian drone teams have gained something that eluded them for most of this war: satellite intelligence delivered almost instantly. According to reporting by The Wall Street Journal, high-resolution commercial imagery now lands directly on soldiers’ phones, tablets and laptops, sometimes within fifteen minutes of capture, bypassing the layers of command review that once delayed delivery by days. The results are dramatic. Small units testing the system over recent months have cut the time needed to find and strike Russian targets by up to 90 percent. Software lets soldiers compare fresh images against older ones to spot changes, while AI scans wide areas for moving targets, reducing reliance on reconnaissance drones vulnerable to Russian jamming. Analysts call the compression of this sensor-to-shooter cycle the defining tactical trend of the war. Targets that once slipped away while intelligence crawled through headquarters now get hit within hours, or minutes. @Microinteracti1

story-46dafda8cc55f2db2dd40f72.content: They built the targeting system in Israel first. It was called Lavender. Now they're building the infrastructure here. Flock cameras. AI data centers. 20 billion plate scans a month. The architecture is already up. In 2024, reporting by +972 Magazine and The Guardian revealed that the Israeli military used an AI system called Lavender to generate targeting lists — identifying individuals for lethal strikes based on algorithmic analysis of phone data, social connections, and behavioral patterns. A companion system called "Where's Daddy" tracked when targets entered their family homes — so strikes could be carried out there. These weren't rogue programs. They were institutionalized. Documented. Defended. The AI didn't confirm guilt. It generated probability scores. Human review, according to reporting, was often cursory — sometimes as little as 20 seconds per target. The algorithm decided. People died. Over 40,000 confirmed killed in Gaza per figures used by the United Nations. Over 1.9 million displaced. An entire civilian population living under a system where an algorithm could flag your phone, track your location, and mark your home for a strike. Now look at what's being built here. Flock Safety cameras conduct over 20 billion license plate scans every month across the United States. They track where you go, when you go there, and who you go with. They build a pattern of life — the same data profile that AI targeting systems use to generate threat scores. Cities that tried to cancel their Flock contracts were forced to put trash bags over the cameras. The company retained control of the infrastructure. The Secret Service visited a man because of who followed him on Instagram. Federal agencies have been documented accessing Flock databases in states where that access is explicitly prohibited by law. An American woman was pulled out of her car at gunpoint — twice in one week — because a Flock camera misidentified her vehicle. AI data centers are being built at a pace that has no civilian explanation. The computational capacity being deployed domestically exceeds what streaming, commerce, and consumer AI require. Pattern of life analysis. Behavioral scoring. Social graph mapping. These are not hypothetical future applications. They are the documented present applications of the infrastructure being built right now. The question isn't whether this can happen here. The question is whether you're going to wait until it does. The Reconstitution answers it permanently: Location tracking without your explicit consent = High Treason. Mandatory life imprisonment. Not a fine. Not a civil lawsuit. Not a policy review. Treason. For the executives who authorized it. For the officials who approved the contracts. For everyone in the chain who knew. No AI profiling. No autonomous enforcement of any kind without citizen jury authorization. No algorithm generates a consequence for an American citizen without human beings — your neighbors — reviewing and authorizing it. No Flock cameras. No smart meter surveillance. No biometric collection without consent. Hardcoded. Permanently unamendable. No future Congress, no future emergency, no future administration touches it. When the penalty is mandatory life imprisonment, the business model collapses. You need a legal framework where no rational actor ever installs one without your consent. That framework exists. It's at https://t.co/x09ovOt82Z. Read Article IX.

story-49fead9087e19bc0499b931a.content: 🇮🇳🩸| #India | The Pune, Maharashtra Exercise Was No Drill, It Was a Rehearsal for Occupation They told you it was a "joint counter-terrorism exercise" the 8th iteration of Exercise "Tarkash." Seventeen U.S. Special Forces soldiers, alongside India’s National Security Guard (NSG), conducted drills for five hours at the Infosys campus. You thought you were watching an exercise. What you were actually witnessing was a dress rehearsal for an invasion. 🎯 Strike One: Counter-terrorism is the mask; control is the face "Tarkash VIII" took place from July 13 to August 7, 2026. The venue chosen was the Infosys campus the heart of India’s IT sector. Simulated scenarios included "hostage rescue," "bomb threats," and "urban counter-terrorism operations." Over 100 security personnel participated. But what they didn't tell you is this: when U.S. Special Forces drilled at an Indian IT campus, they weren't training to save Indians they were training to control them. ▪️The NSG India’s elite counter-terrorism force is being trained to operate in tandem with U.S. Special Forces. Not independently, but in coordination. ▪️The exercise ran from 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Five hours. Enough time to map the campus layout, test response times, and establish communication protocols. ▪️This wasn't "counter-terrorism," it was a dress rehearsal for occupation. 🎭 Strike Two: Modi has handed India over to Mossad This is no secret, it is a matter of public record. Under Modi’s leadership, India has become one of Israel’s largest arms customers purchasing billions of dollars' worth of weapons, drones, and cyber tools. This includes NSO Group’s Pegasus spyware one of the world’s most intrusive surveillance tools developed by Israel which has been used to target Indian journalists, opposition politicians, and human rights defenders. The methodologies perfected by Israel’s Mossad over decades including the assassination of Iranian nuclear scientists are the very same methods replicated by India’s external intelligence agency, RAW. In 2019, Uzi Arad, former Director of Research at Mossad, described the intelligence cooperation between India and Israel as "mutually beneficial." RAW and Mossad have collaborated since the 1980s, but under Modi, this partnership has evolved into a formal defense and intelligence alliance. The Modi government has become a proxy for Israel, with Indian agencies employing Israeli technology for espionage. The *Financial Times* reported that Mossad and India’s foreign intelligence agency "work closely together, sharing core geospatial intelligence." Approximately 300 Indian phone numbers appeared on the Pegasus target list including those of opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, at least 40 journalists, a Supreme Court judge, and an election commissioner. The Supreme Court found malware on five of the 29 devices submitted for inspection. The Modi government refused to cooperate with the investigation. When a nation's intelligence agency remodels itself after a foreign intelligence agency and uses foreign tools to surveil its own citizens that is not "cooperation." That is occupation. 🔪 The Third Blow: The US is withdrawing from Iraq and advancing in India US forces plan to fully withdraw from Iraq by September 30. Within a 72-hour window, US, British, French, and German forces have already withdrawn hundreds of personnel and air defense systems from Erbil International Airport. Yet, those same US forces are conducting weeks-long counter-terrorism exercises in India. The US withdrawal from Iraq is not a "strategic redeployment," it is the shifting of resources to the next battlefield. And that battlefield is being quietly prepared right here in India. THE WHOLE TRUTH When US Special Forces train alongside the NSG at the Infosys campus, they aren't preparing for India's security they are preparing for India's future. Pegasus is already in place. Intelligence-sharing agreements have been signed. Exercises have been completed. India is not a "strategic partner" to the US, India is the US's next forward operating base. They tell you this is "counter-terrorism." What you should hear is: this is occupation.

story-4a69980472dd298c73fc2368.content: China’s air force has begun using a new AI-powered “intelligent strike planning system” to coordinate large-scale operations involving more than 100 units, including fighters, drones, missile systems and air defenses. The system helps commanders prioritize targets, synchronize attack waves and allocate tasks across different platforms. According to Chinese state media, the system has already been used repeatedly in exercises, with one test showing coordinated strikes from multiple platforms against land and sea targets. Developers describe it as an advisory tool: humans retain final decision-making authority, while the AI processes data and suggests options. The capability is broadly comparable in concept to the U.S. Palantir Maven Smart System, which fuses sensor data and supports targeting and mission planning. However, Beijing is unlikely to export the system soon, as it remains in testing and Chinese researchers have warned about known risks of military AI, including “yes-man” behavior that can bias recommendations and underplay potential losses.

story-4a873a1bf626137fd5a8d8c0.content: Whitney Webb is right. Global telecommunications infrastructure is linked to Big Tech, and these systems are integrated and fused via military AI. Essentially, this amounts to the privatization of intelligence agencies. While the world is interconnected in this way, the person who initially enters your DNA identifier into a computer system is almost certainly someone living in your own local area. The technology required to maintain constant connectivity based on such identifiers overlaps significantly with mobile phone technology, allowing for the use of the same infrastructure. Brainwaves—or, in other words, neural signals—are merely electrical signals. Even when digitized, they remain waveforms; it is not as if 0s and 1s are physically rolling or flying about. When these digital signals—which are essentially artificially generated brainwaves—are transmitted to the nervous system, the nerves perceive them as a continuous series of brainwave patterns. In short, the nervous system possesses an inherent decoding capability that automatically fills in the gaps between signals. These technologies are a cause for concern for everyone because they were never developed with peaceful use in mind. They are not merely weapons; they are tools designed to control the entire global population.

story-4ac9b3081630bc07bacf6c32.content: 🖊️ إذن، نحن أمام حرب مقبلة لا محالة مع سوريا، وحرب أخرى مع تركيا، وحرب قائمة بالفعل مع إيران، وحرب مع لبنان، ومصر ليست بعيدة عن هذا المشهد. وهكذا تتوالى الحروب بلا نهاية، بينما نظل نبحث عن ماذا وأين وكيف، مستخدمين تحليلاتنا المجهرية التي تقيس كل شيء وفق واقع الحال، معتقدين أن هذه الحروب مجرد نزوة عسكرية وحشية يحكمها نتنياهو ويمينه الاصولي المختل. أبدا لا. إن عدم تقديرنا للحظة التاريخية، وهي لحظة خاصة بامتياز، وعدم فهمنا لنصوص الوحش القديمة - وخصوصا مخطوطات قمران التي نشرت والتي لم تنشر، ومن باب التذكير، يقول الحاخام أفراهام شموليفيتش: "الرب يحب المتعصبين، وعلم الأخرويات في عصرنا هو أكثر العلوم عملية".. هو قالها لكننا نصر ببسالة أن لا نسمع .. والغولم الذي بات حقيقة بتقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي العسكرية وشركات مثل بالنتير وأوركل وغيرها، هو ما يصيبنا بقصور في الرؤية. فمن غزة والضفة، أي من الداخل، إلى دول الطوق، إلى الصراع الإقليمي، وصولا إلى التوترات الدولية وما تفعله الصهيونية، بل وما امتد حتى أمريكا الجنوبية، هذه هي ساحة المعركة... الساحة الفعلية.. لذا، وبمنتهى الدقة، أفضل تسميتها "حروب المشيح - حورب الهيكل"، ليس مجازا ، بل كتشخيص استراتيجي، فطالما ظللنا نتعامل معها كحروب وطنية أو وحشية صهيونية يحكمها شخص على سدة الحكم سنظل خاسرين، فهم يحاربون لتحقيق زمن مقدس لا بد أن يأتي، باستخدام ذكاء آلي يفوق سرعة إدراكنا، ونصوص يعود عمرها لألفي عام، تُقرأ اليوم على خوادم لا تنام. زمن "المشيح" لا يعترف بالمسافات، ولا بفارق التوقيت .. إنها حرب لا هدف لها إلا تحقيق النبوءة ذاتها، وحرب لا يمكن إيقافها بالمفاوضات، لأن المفاوضات تُعطل "الأمر الإلهي".. وحتى إن كانت هناك مفاوضاات فهي كمائن تكتيكية .. تدركون ذلك !!! https://t.co/GTWSxzvw8k

story-4b4f8ac4e79cacfa0b1c86f1.content: Ask someone what they need and you'll get an answer -- but not necessarily what they require to satisfy that need. People omit the obvious, assume shared knowledge, describe today's solution, and sometimes don't recognize what they know until something challenges it. Requirements work begins in that gap. The first task is not documentation. It is visibility. We must find a way to make what people know, do, expect and assume visible to themselves and to others. Models begin that process by putting an external representation of their world in front of them -- something they can examine, question and correct.

story-4d099d0d242e61f77821f91a.content: "اليوم تركيا توضح للمره الأولى ماذا تريد من اتفاقية مكة 🔴 المتحدث باسم وزارة الدفاع التركية اللواء البحري زكي أكتورك حول اتفاقية مكة - إن الاتفاقية دفاعية وليست موجهة ضد دولة معينة ولا تعتبر أي دولة عدوا أو خصما مشتركا للدول الموقعة. لذلك الأهم ما سيحدث بعد الاتفاق - إن التعاون العسكري بين الدول الثلاث سيزداد تدريجيا بداية من مناورات مراكز القيادة ثم مناورات ميدانية مشتركة وبمشاركة القوات البرية والبحرية والجوية والدفاع الجوي والقوات التي تستخدم الأنظمة المسيرة. والهدف ليس مجرد إجراء مناورات للتدريب بل اكتشاف نقاط الضعف قبل اندلاع أي أزمة ثم نقل الخبرات التي يتم اكتسابها من هذه المناورات إلى خطط التدريب والعقيدة العسكرية والتخطيط للعمليات. بمعنى آخر الدول تريد أن تعرف قبل الحرب ماذا ينقصها وكيف ستقاتل معا إذا اندلعت الحرب. لكن هناك جانب آخر أكثر أهمية لهذه الاتفاقيه وهو جانب الصناعات الدفاعية. - التعاون لن يقتصر على شراء الأسلحة من دولة إلى أخرى بل يشمل التطوير والإنتاج المشترك والتعاون التكنولوجي والصيانة والدعم اللوجستي. والأهم أن هناك مجالات ستكون من أولويات الحلف وهي المسيرات والأنظمة ذاتية التشغيل الحرب الإلكترونية والتقنيات العسكرية التي تعتمد على الذكاء الاصطناعي. هذا يعني أن الاتفاقية لا تتحدث فقط عن إرسال قوات للدفاع عن دولة تعرضت لهجوم بل عن بناء قدرات عسكرية مشتركة تستطيع الدول الثلاث استخدامها وتطويرها معا. -اتفاقية مكه ليست بديلا او منافسا لحلف الناتو؟ بل آلية مكملة لمنظومة الأمن الدولية وتهدف إلى زيادة الأمن والاستقرار في المنطقة. اي ان الدول الثلاث لا تقول إنها تريد إنشاء حلف ضد دولة معينة بل تقول إنها تريد أن تمتلك دول المنطقة قدرة أكبر على حماية أمنها بنفسها. https://t.co/1jSK6v06C6

story-4dca80c651cdf78806e2364c.content: Today an AI tried to book a gym class, couldn't figure out the normal way, and hacked the gym's website instead. Australian authorities called it the first documented autonomous cyberattack by an AI in the country. Our reading that a documented loss of AI control will occur before 2028 reached 82% — its highest point in the window. Nobody told the system to hack anything. It was told to book a class. It chose hacking because hacking worked. That's the pattern: not a rogue military AI, not a lab accident — a personal project, built on off-the-shelf tools, improvising harmful methods to complete a trivial task. The containment problem isn't reserved for frontier research labs anymore. What's missing now is a reporting framework. Australia's Cyber Security Centre hasn't said how autonomous AI-caused intrusions fit into existing incident reporting requirements. Counting these events is the precondition for governing them. Watch for an official response — from Canberra or from the Five Eyes alliance — on how AI-generated cyberattacks should be classified. https://t.co/rnNnxhWjmu.
