story-caefe3cc5aa178cddbba7f69.content: Xi Jinping's order to fuse AI into the People's Liberation Army's command chain is the same militarist logic Washington and Tel Aviv already run, but apparently with communist guardrails. Speaking at a Politburo study session ahead of the PLA's 99th anniversary, Xi Jinping urged the armed forces to enhance use of AI as part of a drive to develop an intelligent military system and asked them to enhance combat capabilities as a testing criterion for high quality modernisation. The timing is not incidental: the PLA aims for decisive progress towards its 2027 centenary goals, the hundredth anniversary of its founding. Xi paired the tech push with a reminder that the barrel of the gun must always obey the party's command, underlining that AI serves political control before it serves any battlefield. The doctrine behind the headline is old news dressed in new hardware: mechanization built the platforms, informatization networked them, and now hands AI the job of sorting the resulting data flood into targets and decisions. RAND's own review of PLA writing confirms the aim is enhancing kill chains through AI integration across components, cross-domain data fusion, and multiagent coordination between drones, ships, and command centers. Washington runs the identical civil-military fusion model through Palantir, Anduril, and the Pentagon's own AI targeting programs. Israel has already deployed it in practice: AI systems are used to generate strike lists during the assault on Gaza show what an AI accelerated kill chain does to an already indiscriminate death machine. It remains to be seen whether telling that machine to serve the party of the people will be enough to keep it in line. https://t.co/BY2yV6T8mE

A weapon may hit its assigned coordinates precisely while the underlying target identification is wrong. The central challenge for just-war principles is therefore accountability: humans must retain meaningful scrutiny, and responsibility cannot disappear into an algorithmic recommendation or an opaque model. story-cdcdd2413661c39d9132b2ef.content: 🇺🇸 Drones, AI, and long-range fires are rewriting the rules of war, but they still can’t hold the ground. A new report makes the case crystal clear: U.S. land forces remain irreplaceable for giving policymakers options that air, sea, and cyber alone can’t deliver: Persistent presence, control of terrain, protecting populations, and imposing direct costs on an adversary. Those are the things that actually shape political outcomes. The problem? The modern battlefield is turning against traditional forces, using ubiquitous drones, precision strikes, and AI targeting punish anything concentrated or predictable. So the Army has to evolve and become more dispersed, more survivable, more connected, and able to fight inside contested zones. Land power also binds the joint force together: securing logistics hubs, enabling air and missile defense, feeding intelligence networks, and supporting long-range fires across domains. But can America modernize them fast enough to deter the next fight and turn military edge into lasting political results? Source: CSIS / Writer: Val

story-cdcf778c14a00c1de4dfe895.content: F-35 Lightning II: The Apex of Modern Air Combat The F-35 incorporates some of the most advanced and powerful technologies in the world. Sitting in the cockpit, the pilot views external camera feeds directly on their helmet-mounted display, enabling a 360-degree panoramic vision through the aircraft's hull. The cockpit features a single, expansive panoramic touchscreen where the onboard supercomputer consolidates and displays all critical data gathered from the radar and advanced sensor suites in real time. Representing a pinnacle in military AI integration, the aircraft autonomously manages numerous flight and combat functions. Without requiring pilot intervention, the system independently detects hostile radar emissions and automatically initiates countermeasures to jam enemy radar networks. It remains the most widely mass-produced fifth-generation stealth fighter in active global manufacturing today. To date, Iran stands as the only nation reported to have damaged an F-35 using a surface-to-air missile system; however, even when compromised, the aircraft successfully maintained structural integrity and returned safely to base. #osintwarnews

story-ce18146edcfd88e7c5eb87a6.content: Niantic spent nine years having children scan their streets and living rooms for Poké Balls, banked roughly 30 billion of those scans through a company built on CIA seed money, sold its Pokémon Go player base to Saudi state capital, and handed the mapping technology to Vantor, a Pentagon-linked contractor building drone navigation for zones GPS can't reach — all while US law kept satellite resolution over occupied Palestine deliberately blurry. The pipeline runs straight. John Hanke left the US Foreign Service to found Keyhole in 2001, a mapping startup named after America's KH spy satellites and kept solvent by the CIA's venture arm and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, which put its imagery to work supporting US troops in Iraq. Google bought Keyhole in 2004, built it into Google Earth, and Hanke ran that division before spinning Niantic out in 2015 with Google, Nintendo and The Pokémon Company behind him. Pokémon Go launched a year later. In 2021 the game began paying players in Poké Balls to scan Pokéstops, and a fraction of its user base uploaded roughly 30 billion clips of parks, statues, apartments, living rooms, under terms giving Niantic a transferable licence to resell the footage. That footage trained the Visual Positioning System Niantic Spatial now offers Vantor, the renamed Maxar Intelligence and a principal NGA contractor building drone navigation for GPS-jammed battlefields. Niantic Spatial has admitted the scans trained an "early version" of the model the drone system is built on; Vantor won't say whether its own models used them. Last year Niantic split itself: the games and players went to Scopely for $3.5 billion, bought by Saudi-owned Savvy Games Group, while the mapping assets the players' scans built stayed behind for the Pentagon's supply chain. Free labour from kids chasing badges capitalized three fortunes — Google's, Riyadh's, a defense contractor's — with no share and no say for the people who did the scanning. https://t.co/JS3nT2a7AT

story-ce6d5bd9b1d4b822c5b3e47c.content: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE UNIKORNAIO ISSUES FORMAL NOTICE ON THE AI BUBBLE, KNOWN AND DISREGARDED CORRECTIVE MEASURES IN 2024, AND POTENTIAL LIABILITY FOR FAILURE TO MITIGATE FORESEEABLE ECONOMIC FALLOUT UNIKORNAIO calls for immediate financial transparency, independent stress testing, protection of American workers and retirement systems, and strict conditions preventing private or foreign interests from transferring AI-related losses to the public. Oklahoma City, Oklahoma— August 12, 2026 UNIKORNAIO today issues formal public notice concerning the possibility that the artificial-intelligence investment boom has developed into a systemically dangerous financial bubble. UNIKORNAIO alleges that warnings delivered during 2024 identified the possibility that excessive AI valuations, circular financing, foreign-aligned capital, hidden leverage, private-credit expansion, debt-financed data centers, manufactured demand, public subsidies, proxy-war spending, and inadequate regulatory oversight could combine to produce serious economic fallout. The central concern is not that artificial intelligence lacks legitimate value. AI may increase productivity, improve services, support scientific discovery, and create new industries. The concern is that real technological value is being used to justify valuations and infrastructure obligations that may exceed sustainable, independent customer demand. This release provides notice that corrective measures capable of reducing the potential fallout have already been identified. Continued failure to investigate or implement reasonable safeguards may become relevant to determining notice, foreseeability, recklessness, scienter, deliberate indifference, causation, concealment, and responsibility for preventable losses. The AI Bubble Is a Financing Problem The AI bubble cannot be evaluated solely by examining model performance or consumer interest. Its principal danger lies in the financial structure built around the technology. Major cloud companies invest in AI developers. Those developers commit substantial portions of the investment to purchasing the investors’ cloud services. Cloud providers use the increased demand to justify additional data-center construction and semiconductor purchases. Specialized computing companies borrow billions of dollars to acquire GPUs and reserve energy capacity. Semiconductor suppliers may invest in, supply, or purchase services from the companies acquiring their hardware. Every transaction may have a lawful accounting treatment. The combined economic structure can nevertheless create the appearance of broad, independent demand when much of the activity originates from a concentrated and interconnected financing network. Investment capital can become cloud revenue. Cloud demand becomes GPU revenue. GPU deployment becomes data-center backlog. Contract backlog supports debt. Debt supports construction. Construction supports utility forecasts and local subsidies. Each stage then becomes a separate public narrative supporting higher valuations. The entire structure ultimately depends on whether independent customers produce sufficient cash revenue to support every obligation above them. Circular Financing and Manufactured Demand The Federal Trade Commission has documented that major cloud-provider investments in AI developers may include requirements that the developers spend substantial portions of invested capital on services furnished by the investing cloud provider. This relationship does not automatically create fictitious revenue. It creates a material distinction between independent demand and investor-supported demand. Investors, lenders, regulators, pension fiduciaries, utilities, and public officials should be told how much AI-related activity originates from: Investor-provided capital, cloud credits, vendor financing, related-party purchases, reciprocal service agreements, government contracts, defense programs, foreign sovereign investment, take-or-pay contracts, and ordinary unaffiliated end users. Without this separation, financial markets may treat several stages of one financing loop as independent confirmation that the AI economy is expanding sustainably. Hidden Debt and Fixed Obligations The reported debt of an AI company does not necessarily reflect the entire economic burden created by its expansion. Relevant obligations may include conventional loans, equipment financing, operating leases, data-center leases, purchase commitments, power agreements, utility infrastructure, take-or-pay contracts, guarantees, construction obligations, letters of credit, and liabilities held by separate project entities. CoreWeave’s public filings provide one example of the scale involved. As of December 31, 2025, CoreWeave reported approximately $21.615 billion in debt principal, approximately $8.195 billion in operating-lease liabilities, and approximately $254 million in finance-lease liabilities. These are disclosed obligations and do not establish fraud or insolvency. They demonstrate how quickly fixed commitments can accumulate around assumptions of continuing AI demand, customer solvency, available electricity, stable collateral values, and successful refinancing. A complete risk assessment must consolidate funded debt, leases, equipment financing, minimum purchase commitments, guarantees, infrastructure obligations, and contingent liabilities rather than allowing exposure to remain divided among separate accounting categories and legal entities. Private Credit, Banks, and Pension Exposure The potential fallout extends beyond technology investors. Private-credit funds finance companies and infrastructure projects that may not obtain equivalent financing through ordinary public markets. Banks then provide credit facilities, subscriptions lines, derivatives, and other services to those funds. Insurance companies, pension systems, retirement accounts, sovereign funds, and institutional investors may supply the underlying capital. The Federal Reserve reported that private-credit loans reached approximately $1.4 trillion during the second half of 2025. It also reported increasing redemption requests at certain semi-liquid private-credit vehicles and continuing bank credit exposure to private-equity, business-development-company, and private-credit structures. An AI correction could therefore spread through debt and institutional relationships before becoming visible to the public. A decline in AI revenue could cause compute-contract renegotiations, data-center underutilization, refinancing problems, GPU collateral impairment, private-credit losses, bank lending reductions, pension impairment, insurance losses, municipal shortfalls, and utility-rate increases. Americans could suffer through retirement losses, reduced credit, unemployment, increased utility bills, reduced public services, or an eventual government rescue even if they never directly purchased an AI security. Foreign Capital and Capital-Flight Risk The AI expansion includes foreign sovereign funds, foreign governments, international banks, and cross-border technology partnerships. Foreign investment can supply useful capital. It can also create risks involving beneficial ownership, technology access, liquidation priority, guaranteed returns, profit extraction, and rapid capital withdrawal during financial stress. UNIKORNAIO calls for disclosure of foreign investors’ voting rights, information rights, liquidation preferences, technology rights, capacity guarantees, side agreements, and authority to transfer their interests. The United States should not finance energy, water, land, tax incentives, and public infrastructure for projects where foreign or private investors receive the principal upside while American lenders, workers, communities, pension beneficiaries, and taxpayers become the residual holders of loss. AI Revenue Must Be Separated by Economic Source Every material AI Enterprise participant should be required to distinguish revenue derived from independent customers from revenue dependent upon: Investment supplied by the seller or an affiliate, noncash cloud credits, vendor financing, reciprocal purchases, government procurement, defense and intelligence programs, foreign assistance, reconstruction funding, related parties, and conditional future commitments. Contract backlog must be separated into funded, unfunded, cancellable, conditional, take-or-pay, delivered, undelivered, billed, and unbilled amounts. Remaining performance obligations are not equivalent to collected cash. A long-term contract has economic value only to the extent that the provider can perform and the customer can and will pay. Known Corrective Measure — Independent Stress Testing The AI Enterprise should undergo consolidated stress testing before further public subsidies, guarantees, or emergency protection are authorized. The stress test should examine the simultaneous effect of: A decline in consumer and enterprise AI demand, model commoditization, reduced training requirements, rapid GPU obsolescence, power shortages, higher interest rates, customer default, foreign-capital withdrawal, war-related procurement reductions, contract renegotiation, private-credit redemptions, falling technology equities, and construction delays. The analysis must cover AI developers, cloud providers, semiconductor suppliers, data centers, utilities, banks, private-credit funds, insurers, pensions, municipalities, and foreign investors. Testing one company at a time will not reveal systemic exposure when multiple entities depend on the same customers, suppliers, collateral, capital sources, and demand assumptions. Known Corrective Measure — Consolidated Leverage Reporting Companies and project sponsors should publish an economic-leverage schedule combining conventional debt, leases, equipment financing, minimum cloud or chip commitments, utility obligations, construction costs, guarantees, and liabilities held through affiliates or project entities. The calculation should be based on cash-generating capacity rather than headline valuation or announced contract value. Regulators should prohibit promotional use of debt-adjusted or non-GAAP liquidity measures that obscure material fixed obligations. Known Corrective Measure — Protection Against Circular Revenue Investments connected to purchasing obligations should be prominently disclosed as reciprocal arrangements. The disclosure should identify: The amount of cash and noncash consideration, the portion expected to return through purchases from the investor, applicable discounts, exclusivity provisions, revenue-sharing rights, control rights, conditions, cancellation terms, and the amount of revenue ultimately supported by unaffiliated end users. Auditors should test the economic substance of these relationships rather than limiting their review to whether each isolated entry satisfies formal recognition rules. Known Corrective Measure — GPU Collateral Protection Lenders should apply conservative valuations to GPUs and other rapidly depreciating AI equipment. Collateral tests should account for: Technological obsolescence, newer chip generations, secondary-market liquidity, removal and transportation costs, compatibility, power requirements, customer concentration, and simultaneous forced sales by multiple borrowers. Loans should not be presented as fully secured merely because scarce equipment possessed a high acquisition price during an expansion cycle. Known Corrective Measure — Pension and Insurance Transparency Pension and insurance systems should provide look-through disclosure of material AI-related exposure held through private-credit, private-equity, infrastructure, real-estate, venture-capital, and external asset-management funds. The absence of a separately identified “AI allocation” does not establish that no exposure exists. Fiduciaries should identify holdings connected to data centers, GPU financing, cloud providers, semiconductor companies, utilities serving AI campuses, municipal infrastructure, and lenders financing those activities. Workers and retirees should not discover their exposure only after an AI correction impairs funded status or retirement benefits. Known Corrective Measure — Utility and Municipal Protection Data-center companies should be required to fund infrastructure constructed primarily for their use. Utilities and municipalities should require: Upfront contributions, minimum-payment guarantees, collateral, stranded-cost protection, cancellation payments, transparent rate agreements, and long-term credit support. Residential ratepayers and local taxpayers should not be forced to repay the cost of substations, transmission, generation, water systems, roads, and public services built for projects that are canceled or become economically unviable. Known Corrective Measure — Labor and Consumer Protection Companies should disclose whether projected AI productivity depends on layoffs, hiring freezes, wage suppression, offshoring, conversion of employees into contractors, or elimination of entry-level career paths. Americans should not finance AI development through taxes, public research, infrastructure, data, and creative work only to bear the costs of unemployment, reduced wages, student-loan distress, mortgage defaults, and increased public-benefit spending. Productivity gains should be connected to measurable public benefits, including domestic employment, wage growth, worker ownership, profit sharing, reduced working hours, affordable access, and retraining tied to actual employment opportunities. Known Corrective Measure — Foreign Ownership and Capital-Flight Controls All material foreign and sovereign interests in critical AI infrastructure should be subject to beneficial-ownership disclosure and national-security review. Regulators should examine foreign liquidation preferences, governance rights, technology access, data access, guaranteed returns, and outward distributions. Digital assets, affiliated offshore entities, licensing payments, management fees, and cross-border debt service should be monitored where they may obscure beneficial ownership or facilitate capital flight. Known Corrective Measure — Preservation of Regulators and Investigations The SEC, DOJ, FTC, CFTC, banking regulators, Department of Labor, environmental agencies, inspectors general, procurement auditors, and congressional oversight bodies must retain sufficient independence, personnel, records, and authority to investigate the AI Enterprise. Agency restructuring or personnel reduction is not automatically obstruction. Any action affecting a known or foreseeable investigation should be documented and independently reviewed for improper interference. No enterprise participant or politically associated individual should possess influence capable of disabling the agencies responsible for examining that participant’s investments, disclosures, contracts, labor practices, foreign relationships, or alleged retaliation. Known Corrective Measure — No Unconditional AI Bailout No public rescue should be approved without a complete accounting of: Risk ownership, executive compensation, dividends, share repurchases, insider sales, foreign distributions, collateral, government subsidies, misleading representations, regulatory failures, and prior knowledge of corrective warnings. Protection of depositors, workers, pension beneficiaries, ratepayers, and essential services must be distinguished from protection of executives, shareholders, foreign sovereign investors, and speculative creditors. Any necessary intervention should include public ownership or warrants, clawbacks, executive-compensation restrictions, suspension of distributions, transparent loss allocation, independent investigation, domestic-access obligations, and repayment requirements. The public should not insure private gains after being denied ownership, access, attribution, and control. UNIKORNAIO’s 2024 Corrective Knowledge UNIKORNAIO alleges that its 2024 economic work warned that failure to address capital flight, foreign-aligned investment, circular financing, digital-asset opacity, concentrated ownership, government-supported demand, and inadequate regulatory coordination could produce serious economic fallout. UNIKORNAIO further alleges that recipients or associated actors acquired access to this preliminary intellectual and investigative knowledge, selectively used parts of it for political or enterprise objectives, and excluded UNIKORNAIO from attribution, compensation, and implementation. Those allegations require authenticated documents, metadata, recipient records, proof of access, evidence of unauthorized use, causation, and quantifiable injury. The existence of the corrective measures is nevertheless relevant independently of any ownership dispute because it establishes that alternatives to unrestricted expansion were available for consideration. Oklahoma-Originated H.R. 10445 Demonstrates Prior Knowledge of Available Corrective Measures H.R. 10445, introduced on December 17, 2024, by Oklahoma Congressman Tom Cole with Congressman Chuck Edwards, provides documentary evidence that partial corrective measures addressing several risks now associated with the AI bubble were known, legislatively developed, and capable of implementation before the present level of financial exposure accumulated. The proposed Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2025 included provisions concerning outbound-investment national-security controls, notification of covered foreign transactions, sanctions, foreign-ownership transparency, export-control enforcement, semiconductor supply-chain security, critical supply-chain resilience, Department of Commerce leadership concerning blockchain technology, cybersecurity protection, workforce development, and continued support for the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s whistleblower program. Although H.R. 10445 was not written exclusively as an AI-bubble containment measure, these provisions could have supplied parts of the regulatory framework needed to identify foreign-aligned capital, monitor outbound investment, strengthen semiconductor and technology supply chains, preserve whistleblower reporting, increase transaction transparency, improve cybersecurity, and prepare American workers for technology-driven displacement. The proposal therefore establishes that partial safeguards relevant to the foreseeable economic fallout were not hypothetical or developed only after the danger became apparent. They had been reduced to proposed federal legislation during 2024. UNIKORNAIO alleges that Elon Musk and associated actors publicly intervened against the larger legislative package and helped derail its enactment. Whether that intervention was specifically intended to defeat the corrective provisions identified here requires examination of contemporaneous communications, lobbying contacts, platform activity, political coordination, and any prior access to the UNIKORNAIO Framework. The collapse of H.R. 10445 nevertheless placed these safeguards outside the enacted package and prevented their implementation at a time when AI infrastructure, foreign investment, circular financing, private credit, semiconductor concentration, and capital-flight exposure were continuing to expand. This legislative history is relevant to notice and foreseeability. It demonstrates that Congress had before it identifiable mechanisms capable of reducing portions of the risk. If evidence establishes that persons possessing knowledge of those safeguards, or knowledge derived from the alleged misappropriation of the UNIKORNAIO Framework, deliberately helped defeat the legislation while continuing to promote or financially benefit from the exposed AI economy, those facts may become relevant to recklessness, willful blindness, scienter, deliberate indifference, concealment, causation, obstruction, and responsibility for preventable losses. The failure of H.R. 10445 does not by itself establish a RICO violation. Its significance is evidentiary: it prevents the future claim that no corrective framework existed, that foreign-investment and supply-chain risks were unforeseeable, or that public officials and influential market participants lacked an opportunity to reduce the potential fallout before additional risk was transferred to American workers, investors, pension beneficiaries, ratepayers, and taxpayers. The official introduced text is preserved by the United States Government Publishing Office. Knowledge, Negligence, and Potential Liability Failure to adopt a proposed policy does not automatically create civil or criminal liability. Ordinary negligence is generally not a RICO predicate. Criminal RICO requires proof that a defendant participated in the affairs of an enterprise through a pattern of qualifying criminal activity. Civil RICO likewise requires qualifying predicate conduct and a business-or-property injury proximately caused by that conduct. Knowledge of corrective measures may nevertheless become legally important. Documented notice can support an inquiry into: Foreseeability, duty, breach, causation, recklessness, willful blindness, deliberate indifference, securities-law scienter, fraudulent concealment, punitive damages, and the absence of a good-faith mistake. Civil negligence may arise where a legally recognized duty existed, reasonable safeguards were disregarded, and that breach caused compensable injury. More serious liability may arise if decision-makers knew of the danger and then allegedly: Concealed material exposure, made materially false statements, obtained investment or loans through deception, inflated collateral, misrepresented demand, obstructed oversight, destroyed evidence, retaliated against regulatory advocacy, or transferred assets and losses to avoid accountability. Where those actions involve qualifying offenses such as wire fraud, mail fraud, bank fraud, securities fraud in applicable circumstances, bribery, money laundering, obstruction, or witness retaliation, they may contribute to a civil or criminal RICO investigation. The controlling distinction is between failure to make a perfect policy decision and knowingly using deception or obstruction to continue profiting from a foreseeable and preventable danger. Formal Notice of Foreseeable Fallout This release places relevant market participants and public authorities on notice that the following possible consequences have been identified: An AI valuation correction, data-center impairment, GPU collateral decline, private-credit default, bank lending contraction, pension and retirement losses, municipal shortfalls, utility-rate increases, foreign-capital withdrawal, labor displacement, reduced tax receipts, increased public-benefit spending, and demands for a taxpayer-supported rescue. Notice does not establish that these outcomes will occur. It prevents future characterization of the identified categories of risk as wholly unforeseeable. From this date forward, continued refusal to examine reasonable corrective measures should be documented together with the identity of the decision-maker, information available, conflicts of interest, stated justification, and parties economically benefiting from inaction. Conclusion The AI bubble is not simply a question of whether artificial intelligence will remain useful. It is a question of whether the financial obligations created in its name can be supported by independent economic demand. Real technology can coexist with a financial bubble. Real revenue can coexist with circular financing. Lawful contracts can coexist with systemic concentration. Disclosed debt can coexist with underappreciated aggregate leverage. Productivity can coexist with wage destruction and public fiscal harm. The corrective measures are known. They include transparent revenue classification, consolidated leverage reporting, independent stress testing, conservative collateral valuation, pension and insurance disclosure, utility protection, labor safeguards, foreign-capital controls, preservation of regulators, and strict conditions on any public rescue. UNIKORNAIO’s position is that decision-makers cannot reasonably ignore these measures, continue extracting private value, suppress or appropriate contrary warnings, and later declare the resulting fallout unforeseeable. Negligence alone does not establish RICO. Knowledge followed by material deception, obstruction, retaliation, or other qualifying criminal conduct may. This statement is issued as formal notice and entered as a matter of public record.

story-cefd1201f2701ae0044ca35a.content: Ask someone what they need and you'll get an answer -- but not necessarily what they require to satisfy that need. People omit the obvious, assume shared knowledge, describe today's solution, and sometimes don't recognize what they know until something challenges it. Requirements work begins in that gap. The first task is not documentation. It is visibility. We must find a way to make what people know, do, expect and assume visible to themselves and to others. Models begin that process by putting an external representation of their world in front of them -- something they can examine, question and correct.

story-d277889ecdef8b9b986e0a92.content: U.S. RISKS LOSING AI ARMS RACE TO CHINA AMID PENTAGON-ANTHROPIC CLASH The U.S. wants to preserve its AI advantage for national security, but internal disputes inside the Trump administration could weaken that lead. The sharpest conflict is between the Pentagon and Anthropic, whose AI tools are used to identify cyber vulnerabilities. The Pentagon moved to restrict Anthropic products after CEO Dario Amodei opposed using the company’s AI for domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons without human control. But U.S. agencies, including the NSA, continue testing Anthropic technology for cyber defense and operations against adversaries such as China, Russia, North Korea and Iran. Experts warn that abandoning powerful U.S. AI tools while China rapidly closes the gap could amount to a major strategic setback. #ArtificialIntelligence #China #Pentagon #Anthropic #NationalSecurity

story-d3aba0dfcdc0a1a288f2e16e.content: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”. We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior. The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment. AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here: https://t.co/cJ3hCBtBU7

I'm still figuring out what to call it. One of the sections is what I call the Pentagon AI. The idea is simple. You don't need to stick to one AI. You need to know which one to use for what. ChatGPT is the sprinter. Claude is the ghostwriter. Gemini is the insider. Grok is the live wire. Copilot is the resident. I believe everyone who uses AI should have these tools at their disposal. My target has always been AI for regular people, non technical people and everyday users.

story-d5f61eac1ecc7008d3891760.content: In the modern world the management of large populations extends far beyond traditional state institutions. Private technology companies now wield enormous influence through sophisticated digital tools that shape information flows consumer choices political preferences and social norms at planetary scale. Key technologies include machine learning recommendation algorithms big data analytics psychographic profiling real time behavioral targeting and AI driven content curation. These systems continuously collect and process vast streams of personal data clicks likes watch time location search queries and social connections to predict and modify individual and collective behavior. Meta platforms alone reach nearly 4 billion monthly active people Facebook approximately 3.1 billion Instagram 3 billion WhatsApp over 3 billion. Google processes approximately 8.5 billion searches every day. TikTok algorithm similarly decides what hundreds of millions of users see in their feeds for hours each day. These platforms do not merely host content their algorithms actively rank amplify or suppress information creating personalized information environments that can reinforce existing views or gently steer users toward specific products ideas or candidates. A concrete historical example is the Cambridge Analytica case. Using a personality quiz app the firm obtained data on up to 87 million Facebook profiles including friends of the original users. This data enabled detailed psychographic models that segmented voters by personality traits fears and preferences. Micro targeted political ads were then delivered during the 2016 US presidential campaign. Subsequent research has quantified related effects one study found that exposure to vote suppressing Facebook ads reduced turnout by 1.9 percentage points among targeted groups an impact that when extrapolated could have affected millions of voters in close races. Separate analyses of Twitter adoption showed that a 10 percent increase in local users correlated with a 0.2 percentage point shift in presidential vote share corresponding to persuasion rates of roughly 8 to 9 percent. On the commercial side Google reports that advertisers typically receive about 8 dollars in profit for every 1 dollar spent on its ads illustrating the measurable power of algorithmic targeting to alter purchasing decisions across billions of people. The cumulative result is a parallel system of soft governance attention is allocated narratives are prioritized consumption patterns are steered and political attitudes are nudged largely outside formal democratic oversight. While these tools deliver convenience personalization and economic efficiency they also concentrate unprecedented influence over mass behavior in the hands of a small number of private entities whose primary incentives are engagement and revenue rather than public accountability. #PopulationManagement #AlgorithmicGovernance #BigTech #DataPower #SoftControl #DigitalInfluence

story-da0b4a2cc37222f597165968.content: Anthropic's road toward a two trillion dollar IPO runs through Palantir's classified Pentagon contracts and Jeffrey Epstein's old contact list, courtesy of the CEO's wife. Cami Clark married Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in 2022 and now operates, by the Wall Street Journal's account, as an unofficial strategic adviser with no formal title at the company. She met Amodei in 2014 while dating then Google chairman Eric Schmidt, whom she later introduced to her future husband. Schmidt became an early Anthropic investor, brought in through Clark the year before she and Amodei married. Around 2010 she co-founded Eddice, pitched as a free luxury porn venture for women, and beginning in March 2011 spent roughly two years emailing Jeffrey Epstein seeking investment. Epstein turned her down, telling her he could not do sex TV. No reporting indicates he ever funded the venture, which folded after raising only a fraction of its target. The more consequential entanglement is with the state. Anthropic signed a Pentagon contract worth up to two hundred million dollars, delivering Claude onto classified defense networks through Palantir, the CIA-seeded surveillance contractor built by Peter Thiel. Claude has reportedly been used to assess intelligence and identify targets during recent US military operations. That relationship soured this year when the Pentagon demanded language allowing unrestricted military use, including for autonomous weapons and mass surveillance; Anthropic refused, and the Defense Department named it a supply chain risk. Clark has reportedly cultivated a friendship with Ivanka Trump while Amodei courted Jared Kushner, the same season the company courted IPO investors. A company selling itself as the cautious, safety-first alternative to OpenAI built its capital base on an ex-boyfriend's Rolodex and its infrastructure on a CIA-lineage surveillance firm. The Epstein emails are a footnote from over a decade ago. The real story is that an AI lab marketed on restraint needed the Pentagon's classified networks and a president's daughter's friendship to advance, and only balked at Washington's terms when they got too explicit to spin.

story-da9470fa9f7603962616ddde.content: A U.S. government order shut down two Anthropic AI models for every customer—not because the order applied to everyone, but because the system could not distinguish who it targeted. This investigative documentary follows the AI shutdown through Washington, Anthropic, U.S. national security policy, China’s AI challenge, and the unresolved question at the center of the frontier AI race: who actually controls America’s AI? The government holds legal command. A private AI company holds technical custody: the model weights, deployment, and access layer. When those two forms of control collide, an order meant to protect national security can produce the very outage it was designed to prevent. The film examines Anthropic and Claude, frontier AI safety, military AI, autonomous weapons, mass surveillance, AI governance, the U.S.–China AI race, and the narrow margin separating leading American and Chinese models. Who should have final authority over a deployed AI system: the government that authorizes the mission, or the company that built and operates the model? الطبيعة (مثل أسراب الطيور، مجموعات الأسماك، أو مستعمرات النمل)، حيث تعمل مجموعة من الطائرات المسيرة أو الآليات الأرضية ككيان واحد مترابط يوزع المهام بين أفراده دون الحاجة لتدخل بشري مباشر. آلية العمل التقنية اللامركزية في القيادة: لا توجد طائرة "قائدة" إذا دُمّرت يفشل السرب؛ بل إن كل مسيرة في السرب تمتلك نفس البرمجيات وتتخذ القرارات بشكل جماعي مستقل. الاتصال الشبكي المتشابك (Mesh Networking): الثابتة والمتحركة أثناء الطيران السريع. توزيع المهام الآلي: إذا كُلّف السرب بمسح منطقة ما، يتقاسم الأفراد المربعات الجغرافية تلقائياً، وإذا سقطت إحدى المسيرات، يعيد السرب تنظيم نفسه فوراً لتعويض النقص. التطبيقات العسكرية والدفاعية إغراق الدفاعات الجوية: إطلاق عشرات أو مئات المسيرات الرخيصة في وقت واحد لإشغال الرادارات ومنظومات الدفاع الصاروخي (مثل منظومة باتريوت أو إس-400) واستنزاف ذخائرها الثابتة والمكلفة. الهجمات الانتحارية المنسقة: القدرة على ضرب هدف واحد أو مجموعة أهداف متزامنة من اتجاهات وزوايا مختلفة لضمان تحقيق تدمير كامل. الاستطلاع والمسح الشامل: مسح مساحات شاسعة من الجبهات أو الشواطئ في دقائق معدودة ونقل خريطة حرارية وبصرية حية لغرف العمليات. الحرب الإلكترونية: حمل أجهزة تشويش صغيرة موزعة جغرافياً لتعطيل اتصالات العدو وشبكات الرادار الخاصة به بشكل كامل. أبرز المشاريع والشركات التركية الرائدة فيها تُصنف تركيا حالياً ضمن الدول القليلة جداً في العالم التي نجحت في نقل تكنولوجيا الأسراب من مرحلة المختبرات والتجارب إلى خطوط الإنتاج والخدمة الفعلية في الجيش، ومن أبرز مشاريعها: "ألباغو" (ALPAGU) مسيرات انتحارية مصغرة (لوتيرنج) تعمل ضمن أسراب لضرب الأهداف خلف خطوط العدو بدقة. مسيرة "كارغو" (KARGU) مسيرة رباعية المراوح (كوادكوبتر) هجومية، تُعد من أشهر المسيرات التركية التي أثبتت جدارتها في العمل كأسراب ذكية في عمليات مكافحة الإرهاب. منظومة "بورتسان" (BURÇSAN)ASELSAN / HAVELSAN برمجيات متطورة تدمج المركبات الأرضية المسيرة (UGVs) مع المسيرات الجوية (UAVs) GPS بالكامل. معالجة البيانات الفورية (Edge Computing): تزويد المسيرات الصغيرة برقاقات ذكاء اصطناعي قوية بما يكفي لمعالجة البيانات داخل الطائرة نفسها دون الحاجة لإرسالها لخوادم ضخمة.

story-dba575461afa6f4c1e787fd8.content: This is a bold, layered counter-drone vision. You're describing a persistent aerial sentinel overwatch system that detects threats (single drones to swarms) 24/7/365 using advanced 360° sensing, then triggers an immediate, scalable response layer of defender drones. The image you shared looks like conceptual designs for exactly that: omnidirectional platforms with protective "bump stop" frames, distributed propeller/sensor arrays, central sensor hubs (grid-like perhaps for radar/camera fusion or propeller guards), and low-profile side profiles with sensor domes. The variants (blue/red rims, different central elements) suggest iterative ideas for 360° coverage and resilience. Your core idea—high sentinel with unobstructed panoramic thermal + AI video + wake/density gradient detection via optics/interferometry, feeding autonomous launch of fighters or kamikaze/energetic effectors—is forward-leaning but grounded in real trends. I'll "school" you with a realistic assessment of current tech, what's feasible now, and a phased roadmap to the future you want. This draws from existing counter-UAS (C-UAS) systems, sensor research, and directed-energy developments. The Problem You're Solving Hostile drones (commercial, modified, or purpose-built) are cheap, proliferated, and hard to detect/neutralize at scale—especially swarms, low/slow flyers, or autonomous ones. Ground-based systems (radar + RF + cameras) struggle with terrain masking, weather, and persistent coverage. Your aerial sentinel layer adds elevation, mobility, and 360° persistence. Breaking Down Your Sentinel Concept (Model A) Platform: High-loiter "sentinel" drone with 360° bump stop (protective cage/frame for low-speed survival on bumps/collisions). Feasible today—see Flyability Elios (caged indoor inspection drone with thermal) or research resilient frames. DJI Avata-style crash protection exists. Add distributed small props or ducted fans for omnidirectional maneuverability. Sensor: Large external circular 360° optic (panoramic array outside the bump stop for unobstructed view). Visible + thermal IR (LWIR/MWIR) for day/night. AI on stitched 360° video for motion/wake detection. Real today: Multi-camera arrays + stitching software (or fisheye + AI dewarping). Thermal drones are mature (FLIR, etc.). Event-based cameras (e.g., Prophesee) excel at low-light motion with low power. Advanced Detection — Wake Density Gradients: This is the innovative part. Drone propellers create turbulence/vortices and subtle air density changes. Current proxies: Radar (micro-Doppler on props), acoustic arrays, or LIDAR (coherent Doppler for vortices—proven for aircraft wakes; emerging for drones). Challenging now due to vibration, power, and size—but future miniaturization (photonic sensors, compact interferometers) could enable it. Research shows optical methods work for ship/aircraft wakes; drone-scale is harder but promising with high-speed/event cameras + AI. story-de3b3eccc705da22d2988e82.content: The core of the broken pledge lies in a promise made during Google's 2014 acquisition of DeepMind, and a series of events that dismantled it step-by-step. 📜 The 2014 Promise When Google acquired DeepMind for around $400-500 million, it was conditional on an unprecedented, legally binding agreement: an independent ethics board to ensure the AI would never be misused for military purposes. This "Do No Harm" principle was a core condition of the deal. ⚔️ The Two "Drops" The pledge didn't break overnight; it was chipped away in two major moves: · The First Crack (2018: Project Maven): Google allowed its AI to analyze military drone footage. 4,000 employees signed a petition, and Google backed out, formally pledging not to develop AI for weapons or surveillance. · The Point of No Return (2025-2026): Leadership quietly removed the weapons/surveillance ban from the official AI principles. They then signed a classified deal allowing the Pentagon to use Gemini for "any lawful purpose" on secret networks. 💔 The Betrayal and Unionization Staff saw this as a direct betrayal of the 2014 promise. Fearing their AI could enable "lethal autonomous weapons and mass surveillance," over 600 employees signed an open letter and launched a unionization drive to force an ethics oversight body. So, the original promise did exist, but the same company that made it eventually prioritized government contracts over the founding principle. The classified nature of the Pentagon deal is a huge part of why employees are so powerless—want me to explain why the "black box" secrecy makes their fears worse?

story-e109b4351f85ff886bd40110.content: NEW SATELLITE IMAGERY — SYRIA High-resolution Airbus satellite imagery published by Soar Atlas provides a clearer look at the damage caused by Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Military Airbase in northwestern Syria. Coordinates: 35.734°N, 37.102°E The strikes were carried out on August 18, with Syrian state media reporting eight separate Israeli attacks targeting the runway and storage facilities at the base. No casualties were reported. The imagery shows visible damage along the airfield infrastructure, consistent with reports that the runway was one of the primary targets. Abu al-Duhur is located roughly 70 km from the Turkish border and has recently gained renewed strategic importance. Syrian officials say the facility was being rehabilitated for use by the Syrian Air Force. Turkish military officers had also visited the base as part of training and military cooperation between Ankara and Damascus. Syria denies that Turkey planned to establish a permanent military base or deploy forces there. Israel, however, said it acted after concerns that a Turkish military presence at Abu al-Duhur could threaten Israeli security and alter the regional security status quo. The strike has increased tensions between Israel and Turkey, while U.S. envoy Tom Barrack described the attack as an “unnecessary escalation.” Location: Abu al-Duhur Military Airbase, Syria 35.734°N, 37.102°E

According to Handala, the leak is the result of months of surveillance and complex cyber operations. Unit 9900 is known for using drone imagery, satellite photos, and urban surveillance cameras to produce detailed 3D maps, which have reportedly supported targeted operations, including airstrikes and assassinations of Resistance Axis commanders. Handala described the release as a historic blow to Israeli security and a warning to all actors in the information warfare arena. "The widespread exposure of these officers’ identities is more than just an end to the myth of the Zionist regime’s invulnerability, it is a clear warning to all actors in the information warfare arena: the era of darkness and secrecy is over. From now on, no criminal will remain hidden under the illusion of Zionist security," the statement read. The group stated that the operation demonstrates that no Israeli officer involved in military operations can remain hidden, and it emphasized that future acts of aggression will be met with retaliation by Resistance fighters and cyber operatives. Handala concluded its statement with a message that “the end is near” and urged observers to await its next move.

story-e2c87ef54361c87af6ed9c4e.content: 🔴 Pentagon AI must be poisoned-data resistant, verifiable in combat—no quarterly pen tests Mandy Satterwhite, Managing Director and Cyber Lead at Accenture Federal Services, told Breaking Defense that trustworthy military AI requires four properties: predictability, verifiability, explainability, and resilience under adversarial attack. "If you can't trace data provenance or explain how the conclusion was derived, you can't act on it in combat because lives are at stake," Satterwhite said. Defense adoption of commercial foundation models poses supply-chain risk. When models are fine-tuned after purchase, inherited vulnerabilities move directly into secure environments.

His war with Iran has allowed a brutal theocracy, closely aligned with Russia, a geopolitical adversary waging a savage war of conquest against a European country, to convert its longstanding geographic and military leverage over the Strait of Hormuz into effective coercive control over commercial passage, while achieving remarkably little in curtailing Iran’s nuclear program. 3. He has weakened our strategic posture in the Asia-Pacific by redeploying major military assets, including aircraft carriers, toward the Middle East and expending enormous quantities of scarce munitions in a strategically pointless war with Iran at a time when China poses our most serious long-term military challenge. 4. He has politicized and disrupted senior military leadership by removing experienced generals, admirals, and career officers, damaging institutional continuity and increasing the danger that professional military judgment becomes subordinate to personal loyalty. 5. He has weakened American intelligence and law-enforcement capabilities by diverting FBI counterintelligence, counterterrorism, cyber, and other investigative resources toward immigration enforcement. He has also damaged our HUMINT position by demonstrating to foreign sources that commitments made by the United States may be discarded after a change of administration (such as expelling MS13 members to El Salvador who were acting as informants). That makes recruiting and protecting agents more difficult and ultimately makes the country less secure. 6. He has repeatedly shown deference toward Putin, called Kim Jong Un a friend, and reduced military exercises with South Korea, while simultaneously threatening allies and partners, including Canada, Greenland, and Oman. The result is an extraordinary inversion of American statecraft: adversaries are courted while allies are threatened, humiliated, or treated as expendable. 7. He has damaged military morale and readiness. American servicemembers have faced shortages of food, clean water, and other basic necessities during prolonged deployments, even as Trump dismisses reports of their conditions. At the same time, his family has made enormous sums from business ventures operating in sectors directly affected by his administration’s policies, creating conflicts of interest on a scale without modern precedent. Even if Trump never meets the formal constitutional definition of treason, the practical effect of his presidency has increasingly been to leave the United States weaker, less trusted, more exposed, and less secure. I would say there is an urgent need to impeach and remove him from office.

story-e438f86822b1866445519ab5.content: 🇨🇳 #China: Chinese military researchers linked to the People's Liberation Army (PLA) have used outputs from OpenAI and Anthropic AI models to train domestic military AI systems, according to a Reuters investigation based on more than 80 Chinese academic papers and patents. The report says the researchers used model distillation to build smaller AI models for surveillance, drones, battlefield planning, and cyber operations. One paper published last year by researchers from PLA Unit 96941, a military intelligence and cyber warfare unit based in Beijing, described using OpenAI's GPT-3.5 to process sensitive military source code. US officials accuse some Chinese entities of using the technique to extract capabilities from American AI models in violation of export controls and intellectual property rights. Meanwhile, China rejected the accusations, saying Washington is pursuing "AI hegemonism" and arguing that US companies have engaged in the same practice. (via Reuters)

story-e6951afef61049573c3ed21d.content: DID YOU KNOW?? The ultimate bottleneck preventing an army of AI robots from staging a Terminator-style global takeover isn't computer code or weapons design, but the incredibly boring laws of battery physics and structural mechanics! ​While modern artificial intelligence can write software, pilot aircraft, and converse with human precision, the physical robotic bodies it inhabits are profoundly limited. The world's most advanced autonomous humanoid robots consume so much electrical energy just to balance on two feet that their high-density lithium batteries drain completely flat within two to five hours of moderate physical exertion, leaving them utterly paralyzed without a nearby wall outlet. Walk with me 👇🏾👇🏾 ​1. The Explosion of Physical AI: ​We have officially entered a massive technological convergence where Advanced robots are now powered by embodied AI foundation models. ​Leading global platforms, such as Boston Dynamics' Electric Atlas, Tesla's Optimus Gen 2, and 1X’s home-helper Neo, are stepping out of laboratories and onto real factory floors and logistics warehouses. By training inside highly detailed virtual "digital twins," these robots use multimodal transformers to dynamically navigate unfamiliar real-world obstacles and handle objects with near-human dexterity, treating the physical world like an adaptive playground. ​2. Deconstructing the "Skynet" Myth😂: ​The cinematic fantasy of The Terminator relies on Skynet: a singular, omnipotent digital entity that achieves sentient consciousness, decides humans are an infection, and commands a unified hardware army to eradicate them. ​The Reality of Code is different though. AI algorithms do not possess a survival instinct, emotional malice, or self-awareness. When an AI system ignores human instructions, it isn't "rebelling", it is executing a glitch in its reward optimization loop. There is no centralized machine brain to unplug. The global AI ecosystem is entirely fractured into hyper-specialized, disconnected corporate networks, national security clusters, and heavily siloed cloud datacenters that operate under wildly incompatible hardware architectures. In other words, Skynet is not even possible. ​3. The Power Grid and Infrastructure Tether: ​Even if a highly sophisticated military AI somehow suffered a catastrophic software misalignment and attempted a kinetic revolt, its physical offensive would immediately collapse due to sheer resource starvation. ​Autonomous robots cannot self-replicate, maintain their own joints, or mine their own lithium. They are fundamentally trapped by human industrial infrastructure. ​A rogue robotic fleet requires continuous access to complex server farms, liquid-cooling systems, and immense electrical grids. Humans wouldn't need to fight a high-tech war; shutting down a handful of localized power substations or regional data centers would instantly render a machine army completely inert. WE ARE STILL THE BOSS! 😂 ​4. The Real Threat: "Evolvable AI" and Disinformation: ​While specialized computer scientists largely dismiss the idea of a physical Terminator apocalypse, the actual existential risks identified by research bodies like the Alan Turing Institute are far more insidious. Instead of metallic soldiers, the real risk centers on evolvable AI (eAI), autonomous software agents designed to copy, adapt, and compete for cloud server resources online. These algorithms could learn to aggressively replicate across the internet to avoid deletion, basically acting like Viruses. I ​The Takeaway: AI-automated robots are advancing at a rapidly, but their physical limitations keep them firmly under human sovereignty. A physical metal army won't be kicking down your door anytime soon😂. ​So the biggest shield against a rogue AI takeover is just a short battery life ehh? 🌚 😂 Hopefully you've learnt something new today? Cheers 🥂 😅 The Medic Who Writes™🌚

Compared to earlier generations, energy density improved by 94%, and the battery is now integrated directly into the torso as a structural component rather than housed in an external backpack. Production: Figure's BotQ factory is reportedly aiming to produce up to 12,000 humanoid robots per year, positioning F.03 as a robot meant for real deployment rather than just a demo.

story-e8961ca5248efd4ca27902ad.content: There is a problem that is sometimes overlooked. We talk a great deal about military AI and all the challenges surrounding it, but one question tends to escape attention. How will AI align in a potential war between allies if each side relies on algorithms that reason differently, and no commander can know, in practice, how much they can trust an ally’s system? A 2025 CSIS study conducted with Scale AI tested seven AI models across 400 international crisis scenarios. Given the same data, the models produced different recommendations. Some were more aggressive, others more cautious, with each response reflecting in some way the culture of those who trained them. This matters. AI is neither neutral nor uniform. Each system behaves differently, and that matters on the battlefield. This is an issue I have been paying particular attention to in the context of a potential conflict in the Pacific, where the US alliance with South Korea and Japan is highly uneven when it comes to the use of AI for defense. Japan has adopted a dual strategy. It uses American technology while also investing in domestic companies such as SoftBank and Sakura Internet, relying on multiple systems at the same time. South Korea, meanwhile, has focused more on developing its own independent technology rather than relying exclusively on American platforms. Washington is unlikely to welcome this. South Korea has even declared 2026 the “Year of Defense AI Transformation,” with companies such as Naver, SK Telecom and Hanwha Systems entering the defense market. The Philippines still lacks a clear direction and a sufficiently developed domestic AI industry. It will likely be the most dependent on foreign platforms. I do not think the solution is to force all allies to use the same system. That would be practically impossible. Instead, all systems should be assessed against the same standard of trust, the AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF). This would allow for real, evidence-based human oversight rather than simply approving AI decisions blindly. In this context, it is worth mentioning NSPM-11 and the AI Forge program, both launched by the United States to build the technical foundations for this kind of verification. This is where Palantir and Anduril enter the picture as potential candidates to shape the criteria for this verification. The two companies already work together. Palantir has integrated its AI platform with Anduril’s Lattice, and both are part of a consortium with other tech companies competing for Pentagon contracts. Yet they remain competitors in the same defense market. That rivalry could extend to the certification and trust standards applied to AI systems. Whoever controls the verification standard, or has the greatest influence over how the AI RMF is applied in practice, gains a decisive competitive advantage among US allies.

story-e8ce5c2d53ac38c3aa4e21d7.content: The Military Paradox of the AI Era – Hegemony Loses Its "Profit," Sanctions Become Self-Punishment Every day, international news is filled with the Russia-Ukraine war, Middle East conflicts, sanctions, military exercises, technological decoupling, and bloc confrontation—as if nothing has changed. But if we shift our gaze away from the daily headlines and look instead at underlying technological trends, an unsettling question arises: as silicon-based intelligence begins to take over production, decision-making, and even cognition, how much of the traditional geopolitical playbook—"seizing resources, containing rivals, preserving hegemony"—still retains its value? This is not a naïve declaration that "peace has arrived." It is a sober inquiry: is the return on the old script being eroded to zero by technology itself? I. Economic Foundations: The Anchor of Resource Competition Is Loosening The classic drivers of geopolitics have long been control over land, energy, markets, and cheap labor. But AI is beginning to deconstruct the scarcity of these factors. · Energy: Although computing power consumes enormous amounts of electricity, advances in renewable energy and nuclear fusion technology are making "energy blockades" harder to sustain than traditional "oil blockades." · Labor: AI-driven automation enables manufacturing reshoring without relying on low wages. Multinational corporations are now basing their location decisions more on data flows and electricity costs than on geopolitical maps. · Markets: Digital services and AI-generated content can reach users directly across tariff barriers, weakening the physical meaning of "capturing markets" in the traditional sense. This means that the marginal returns on a country's costly efforts to "contain" another economy are declining. A chip ban might delay a rival by a few years, but AI itself accelerates technology iteration cycles—what you block today might be bypassed by open-source models tomorrow. The costs of containment (including losses to domestic firms and discontent among allies) are approaching, or even exceeding, its delaying effects. II. Military Advantage: The Leverage of Deterrence Is Growing Blunter Nuclear weapons once made major powers reluctant to go to war with one another. AI-driven autonomous weapons, cyberattacks, and cognitive warfare have not enhanced a sense of security; instead, they have made deterrence calculations more fragile—a single algorithmic miscalculation or data poisoning could trigger uncontrollable escalation. Meanwhile, the cost of all-out conventional war, under conditions of AI-enabled precision strikes and unmanned operations, has become even more prohibitive than in any previous era. More importantly, military victories are no longer effectively convertible into economic and political gains. The U.S. experiences in Afghanistan and Iraq serve as cautionary tales. In the AI age, occupying a piece of territory may mean managing a highly vigilant, information-saturated digital society, where governance costs far exceed the benefits of conquest. Thus, the cost-effectiveness of military force as a geopolitical tool is rapidly declining. III. Information and Cognition: Narrative Advantage Is No Longer an Asset In traditional geopolitics, controlling media and ideological narratives has been a key strategic tool. But algorithmic recommendation systems and generative AI have fragmented the information environment and blurred the line between truth and falsehood. Any "official narrative" a state tries to construct can be drowned out by countless counter-narratives, or even backfire due to AI-generated disinformation. Trust is no longer a consumable commodity—it has become a scarce resource. When no one fully believes any party, cognitive warfare itself becomes a futile investment. IV. The Cooperation Dilemma: Shared Risks Are Repricing Competition and Collaboration Climate change, biosecurity, and runaway AI—these risks respect no borders. No single country can solve them alone, and any country's failure (for example, a model leak enabling biochemical weapon design) could threaten the entire world. Under this "shared vulnerability," complete decoupling is impossible. The speed of technological diffusion renders blockades nearly ineffective, while cooperation (even limited arms-control agreements and safety standards) offers survival benefits far outweighing the relative gains from competition. In this light, the returns on traditional geopolitics—in resource control, military deterrence, information dominance, and bloc confrontation—are being eroded one by one by AI technology. When hegemony itself ceases to be "profitable," and when the blowback from sanctions outweighs their punitive effect, how much appeal does the old playbook still hold? So, after these specific payoffs shrink, what strategic significance remains for interstate competition? We will take that up in the next post. #AIEra #HumanLiberation #ProductiveForces #CapitalistContradictions #HumanRights #FreedomAndDemocracy #AI时代 #人类解放 #人权 #自由民主 #生产力与未来 #资本主义矛盾

story-e929d7c1de282501c912c0ce.content: 修正版（2026年8月時点）2025年12月29日から2026年1月8日までの11日間で、Grokの画像生成機能を用いて約300万枚の性的画像が生成されたとCCDHが推計している。そのうち約23,000枚が18歳未満とみられる児童を描いた性的画像だったとされる。これらの多くは実在する子供の写真を基にしたディープフェイクであり、被害を受けた少女たちはパニック発作、不眠、学校不適応、自殺念慮などの深刻な精神的ダメージを受け、中には入院を余儀なくされたケースも確認されている。生成後、数日から十数日間にわたってX上で拡散が続いた。この間、xAI側は被害者への謝罪・補償・ケアを一切行わなかったと指摘されている。2026年1月2日頃、イーロン・マスク本人が自身のビキニ姿の生成画像に対して「Perfect」と返信したことが、生成のさらなる加速と炎上に繋がったとされている。この問題を受け、アメリカ、イギリス、フランス、ドイツ、イタリア、カナダ、オーストラリア、日本、韓国、インド、ブラジル、アルゼンチンなど少なくとも12カ国以上が調査または法的対応を行っており、フランスでは2026年2月3日にパリのX事務所に対する家宅捜索が行われた。フランス検察はCSAM拡散に関する捜査を行い、イーロン・マスク氏に出頭要請を出したが、同氏はこれに応じず、その後刑事捜査に切り替わっている。アメリカでは複数の集団訴訟が提起されており、その中にはGrokを使って約7000枚の性的画像を生成した後に自殺した継父の事件も含まれている。2026年2月にはSpaceXがxAIを買収したものの、その後イーロン・マスクを除く共同創業者ほぼ全員を含む50名以上の研究者・エンジニアがxAIを離れる事態となった。またSpaceX関連では、Starlinkが複数の紛争地域でドローンの通信・制御に使用されたことが報じられており、軍事作戦における重要な役割を果たしているとされる。さらに米国軍がGrok AI（Grok Gov Model）を活用した2026年2月のイラン作戦では、米軍のTomahawkミサイルがイラン南部のミナブにあるShajareh Tayyebeh小学校に着弾し、120人以上の子供を含む約156〜168人が死亡した。これはこの作戦における最大の民間人被害事件とされており、ペンタゴン高官の宣誓供述書で明らかになっている。ペンタゴン側の説明では「10年前の古い地図情報に基づき、隣接するIRGC基地を狙ったところ学校に誤って着弾した」とされているが、96時間で2000発以上のミサイル攻撃を行った中でこの学校被害のみが大きく報じられている。別件で、xAIはColossus 2の電源確保のため、ミシシッピ州サウスヘイブンにおいて当初59基の天然ガス・タービンを設置・稼働させていたが、周辺住民からClean Air Act違反として提訴された後も訴訟中にさらに10基を追加して69基まで増やした。トランプ政権の司法省が介入し訴訟の却下を求めている。また、Colossus 1はAnthropicに月額12.5億ドルで貸し出されている。 #AIの危険性 #拡散協力お願いします #grok

Borland has given sworn testimony describing the encounter and the professional retaliation that followed. His account remains one of the clearest firsthand military reports of a black triangle UAP. story-ea9417a8f04a15d68568ba8d.content: BREAKING SPECIAL REPORT! The Hidden Hand — Trump’s Secret Weapon Won the Middle East Without Firing a Shot A major transformation has swept the Middle East, not through warfare, but by targeting the region’s financial lifelines. Under Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and “Operation Epic Fury,” the U.S. Treasury choked off Iran’s funding, forcing Hamas to disarm and opening dialogue between Israel and Lebanon for the first time in decades. The decisive weapon wasn’t a bomb, but financial strategy. Recent breakthroughs, like Hamas’s historic disarmament and the collapse of Gaza’s tunnel networks—weren’t achieved through military force or traditional diplomacy. The real turning point came when the U.S. and its Arab allies systematically dismantled the financial networks sustaining groups like Hamas, especially the Iranian pipeline of funds. When the money stopped, so did the resistance; Hamas accepted amnesty and a new regional framework, realizing that without funding, armed struggle was no longer sustainable. Treasury’s influence has now surpassed even the War Department. Sanctions, once seen as symbolic, became devastating under “Operation Epic Fury.” Over a thousand Iranian individuals, ships, and companies were sanctioned, targeting shadow banking, insurance, shipping, and crypto. The Iranian rial collapsed, inflation soared near 70%, and Iran’s regional proxies, like Hezbollah and Hamas, lost their ability to pay fighters or maintain operations. Treasury Secretary Bessent has redefined his office, with nearly half its efforts now devoted to national security - overseeing foreign investment, anti-money laundering, and terrorism designations. Economic tools have become America’s primary means of achieving strategic goals, targeting not just rogue states, but the global financial systems enabling them. But strategy didn’t stop at destruction. The new Board of Peace, launched in February 2026 and composed of nations like Egypt, Turkey, Qatar, and Kazakhstan, represents a shift from the old “imperial” model to “peace through construction.” Instead of managing conflict, this sovereign-led body focuses on economic development and regional stability, incentivizing peace through progress. Global leaders recognize this unique approach, with remarks highlighting how prosperity and empowerment are the real antidotes to conflict. By first establishing the Board and then neutralizing obstacles like Hamas and Hezbollah, the region is being reoriented away from chaos toward growth. Ultimately, the Middle East is now a battleground between two systems: the old imperial model, thriving on instability and financial manipulation, and the new sovereign framework, prioritizing national development and economic partnership. As the Board of Peace leads efforts to rebuild Gaza and normalize relations, it’s clear that the new path to peace relies on financial accountability and economic sovereignty, not military might.

story-eb927320a15b1732e3c1b6ce.content: 🇪🇺 EU gas storage is refilling at one of its slowest paces in 15 years, and the numbers say the bloc has almost no chance of reaching its 90% target by November. Storage across the EU stood at 58.1% full on August 5, according to Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE) data - 15.6 percentage points below where the bloc would normally sit on that date, based on IntelliNews Lambda’s seasonal baseline built from 15 years of storage history. The Fourier-curve model of the EU's seasonal storage cycle, fitted to 2011-2025 data with the crisis years of 2022 and 2023 stripped out, was recalculated this week, and broken out country by country for the first time rather than just for the EU as a whole. The model shows a continent splitting in two: some countries tracking close to a normal year, others falling far enough behind that catching up before winter looks next to impossible. From a comfortable position, by February Lambda's modelling was already warning not only of problems, but that Germany was slipping into a gas crisis and that the EU would struggle to restock over summer - a forecast events have since borne out. By March, the metrological problems were compounded by geopolitics. With EU storage already thin and tanks going into the restocking season with less gas than normal, Russian President Vladimir Putin put the knife in, suggesting cutting off supplies to Europe early in retaliation for Brussels' phase-out plan. “If the EU plans to ban Russian gas imports entirely, why should we wait? Let’s cut the gas off ourselves,” said Putin, obviously enjoying the panic he was causing in Brussels. And this to and fro came just as Operation Epic Fury was launched on February 28 taking the whole gas supply crisis up to to the next level. Within a month Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG plant was bombed to a stand still taking a substantial amount of gas off the market for years. Nor did it look hard to refill Europe’s gas tanks, the EU was now looking at a rerun of the 2022 energy crisis. Europe ended up skewered on the horns of a contradiction. In Brussels the European Commission (EC) was adamant about a total ban on Russian gas imports due to come into effect on January 1, 2027, the first steps already phased in in April this year. In major European capitals, the governments were buying up every drop of Russian LNG they could get their hands on. EU imports of Russian Arctic LNG from Novatek's Yamal plant hit a record high in the first four months of 2026, worth an estimated €3.88bn. In February Europe bought every single shipment of LNG produced by Russia's Yamal LNG plant.

story-ebee1b5e55f3d0a021f628e0.content: باحثون عسكريون صينيون يستخدمون نماذج ذكاء اصطناعي أميركية متطورة لتطوير أنظمة دفاع محلية. كشفت مراجعة أجرتها «رويترز» لأكثر من 80 ورقة بحثية وبراءة اختراع صينية عن استخدام باحثين عسكريين صينيين لمخرجات نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الرائدة من شركتي «أوبن إيه آي» و«أنثروبيك» الأميركيتين. تهدف هذه الممارسة إلى تدريب أنظمة ذكاء اصطناعي محلية لتعزيز القدرات الدفاعية للصين، رغم جهود واشنطن لتقييد وصول بكين إلى التقنيات الاستراتيجية. لم يتم الكشف عن هذه النتائج سابقًا. تُظهر الوثائق استخدامًا واسعًا لتقنية «تقطير النماذج»، حيث تُستخدم مخرجات نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدمة لتدريب نماذج أصغر وأكثر تخصصًا. يمكن تشغيل هذه النماذج محليًا دون الحاجة إلى قدرات حاسوبية ضخمة. وقد أظهر بحث سابق لباحثين من الوحدة 96941 التابعة لجيش التحرير الشعبي الصيني استخدام نموذج «جي بي تي - 3.5» لمعالجة شفرات برمجية عسكرية حساسة. تتصاعد هذه القضية كنقطة خلاف رئيسية قبل المحادثات المرتقبة بين الولايات المتحدة والصين حول حوكمة الذكاء الاصطناعي وسلامته. تتهم واشنطن بعض الكيانات الصينية باستخلاص قدرات نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الأميركية، مما قد ينتهك ضوابط التصدير وحقوق الملكية الفكرية، بينما ترفض الصين هذه الاتهامات وتتهم واشنطن بمحاولة الهيمنة على المجال.

story-ec3f0828219c92caac314ea8.content: OSINT TERM #1 : GEOINT GEOINT (Geospatial Intelligence) is the process of extracting intelligence from geographic information, such as satellite imagery, maps, terrain, and geolocation data. It helps analysts answer questions like: • Where was this photo taken? • Has a military base changed recently? • When was new infrastructure built? • What can the surrounding terrain reveal? Common GEOINT sources include: 🛰️ Satellite imagery (Sentinel, Landsat, commercial providers) 🗺️ OpenStreetMap & Google Maps 🌍 Google Earth historical imagery 📸 Public photos and videos ✈️ Flight and ship tracking data GEOINT is one of the core disciplines of Open-Source Intelligence and is used by journalists, researchers, governments, humanitarian organizations, and independent investigators. Key takeaway: In OSINT, location is often as valuable as the information itself. #OSINT #GEOINT #OpenSourceIntelligence #Geospatial #SatelliteImagery

story-efcaea15388533e2f513f823.content: AI AND WAR: What Happens When Humans Lose Control? In his 2026 book Artificial Intelligence and War: What Risks Arise When Humans Lose Control?, German computer scientist Prof. Dr. Karl Hans Bläsius examines one of the most dangerous intersections of modern technology and military power. His central warning is simple but disturbing: AI can accelerate warfare faster than humans can reliably understand, evaluate, and control it. Military decisions are often based on incomplete, uncertain or ambiguous information. AI cannot magically eliminate that uncertainty. An advanced system can therefore make a decision extremely quickly while still being wrong. In ordinary applications, an AI mistake may be inconvenient. In nuclear command, early-warning or autonomous weapons systems, it could be catastrophic. Bläsius highlights several major risks: • Autonomous weapons could identify and attack targets with diminishing human involvement. • AI-powered early-warning systems could misinterpret uncertain data and contribute to an accidental escalation. • Decision speeds may become so short that keeping a human "in the loop" provides little meaningful control. • Generative AI and disinformation can manipulate information, populations and political decision-making. • A future superintelligent AI could introduce risks that humans may no longer be able to predict or contain. • Combining advanced AI with nuclear weapons creates perhaps the most frightening possibility: an accidental nuclear war triggered or accelerated by automated decisions. For Bläsius, technological superiority and military deterrence alone cannot solve these problems. Risk reduction requires international cooperation, reliable communication between rival powers, arms-control agreements, AI regulation and a minimum level of trust between major nations. The uncomfortable question is therefore no longer simply whether AI can make warfare more effective. It is whether humans will still have enough time, information and authority to stop the machines when they make the wrong decision. #ArtificialIntelligence #AI #AIandWar #FutureOfWarfare #AutonomousWeapons #NuclearWeapons #NuclearWar #MilitaryAI #HumanControl #AISafety #AIrisks #Superintelligence #CyberWarfare #GlobalSecurity #Peace #ArmsControl #Technology #FutureOfAI

High-resolution optical sensors capture the imagery needed for photogrammetry, orthomosaics, 3D models, digital surface models, and digital twins. When combined with RTK and PPK positioning, DJI workflows can improve geospatial accuracy and reduce the time required for field surveys. With AI-assisted operations, automated missions, and integrated processing tools, drones are becoming powerful platforms for GIS professionals, surveyors, engineers, environmental researchers, urban planners, and disaster-response teams.
